approaches_tried: Modeled the deny_json JSON form, PROJECT_ROOT anchoring, and fail-open command-substitution idiom directly on enforce-scope.sh.template rather than inventing a new convention -- matches this repo's copied-then-project-owned hook pattern.

Check 0's compound-stage-and-commit detection distinguishes two real attack shapes (git add && git commit; git commit -a/-i/--all/--include, including combined short-flag clusters like -am) from the documented false-positive case (a commit message merely mentioning 'git add') by stripping quoted spans before pattern-testing -- manually verified against -am, git commit <pathspec> (residual hole, correctly passes), and --amend with nothing staged (correctly passes).

Check 1's git diff --cached -U0 output has no context lines by construction, so a running line counter seeded from each hunk's @@ header can't drift -- avoided the more error-prone approach of tracking context vs added lines separately.

Added RV's non-blocking recommended test (exception-logging type-name-only contract) by staging genuinely invalid UTF-8 bytes, which forces a real UnicodeDecodeError when git diff --cached output is decoded -- verified against the actual exception path, not a mocked one.

F006/OVI-62's harness-doctor commit-gate probe test (DIR_DOC_GATEMISSING) broke once this template became real, since install_hooks() now copies it into every fixture automatically -- fixed by explicitly removing the copied file to restore that test's 'not yet copied' precondition.

Adversarial review of the first PR pass found a CRITICAL bug: a staged line that happened to start with '++ ' (e.g. content from a staged .patch/.diff file) was mis-parsed as a real diff file header, both leaking staged content into the denial message and letting a forged '*.env.example'-shaped fake path skip the rest of the scan entirely -- a total Check 1 bypass. Fixed by gating header detection on being outside a hunk (in_hunk tracking, reset on 'diff --git'). Also found: the secret pattern's \b keyword boundaries missed SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE identifiers (AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY) and JSON-quoted keys entirely (the dominant real-world secret shape); 'git -C . commit' and 'git stage' both bypassed detection; url-credential was http(s)-only. Fixed all 4, then independently reproduced each exploit against the fixed code before writing formal regression tests, and mutation-tested the two most security-critical new tests (temporarily reverting to the buggy code, confirming they fail, then restoring) rather than trusting that a passing assertion proves the fix. Re-measured coverage via the stdlib trace module (replaying all test scenarios, including a fake slow 'git' binary to force the real TimeoutExpired path via a COMMIT_GATE_DIFF_TIMEOUT testability knob): 90.1% (reviewer's measurement) -> 100%.

Second security re-review found 2 more MAJOR findings introduced by the first round's own fixes: (1) COMMIT_PATTERN/STAGE_PATTERN's '.*' between 'git' and the subcommand matched 'commit'/'add' as bare substrings of filenames ('git add commit-gate-helper.sh') and branch names ('git push origin add-feature'), denying commands that were never staging-and-committing at all -- fixed by requiring the subcommand be its own whitespace-bounded token, not just a \b-delimited substring (\b alone still matches inside 'commit-gate.sh' since '/' and '-' are non-word chars), and excluding command-separator chars from the wildcard so a match can't span into an unrelated later command. (2) The widened SECRET_PATTERN's leading wildcard prefix created real polynomial-time backtracking on adversarially repeated keyword-shaped text (reproduced independently, though at a more modest magnitude than the reviewer's own measurement -- reported honestly rather than repeating an unverified number) -- fixed by anchoring the pattern directly on the keyword (dropping the ambiguous prefix quantifier) and adding a hard length cap on the scanned span as defense in depth, bounding worst-case time regardless of the pattern's exact complexity. Both false-positive regression tests were mutation-tested (reverted to the pre-fix regex, confirmed to fail, then restored).

Third security re-review confirmed the round-1 CRITICAL fix and the round-2 fixes were correct, but found the round-2 regex tuning (\bgit\b[^|;&]*(?:^|\s)commit(?:\s|$)) had introduced TWO more regressions in the same two lines: the wildcard spans newlines (letting an unrelated later line's 'add' token pair with an earlier line's 'git', denying e.g. 'git commit -m x' followed by an unrelated 'pnpm add' on the next line), and the (?:\s|$) terminator lets a genuine compound command with no whitespace around a separator bypass detection entirely ('git add .;git commit;git push' -> silently allowed). The reviewer named this pattern explicitly: three rounds of regex tuning, each fixing the reported case while introducing a new one in an untested dimension -- and recommended replacing the regex-based subcommand detection with a real tokenizer. Rather than risk a round-5 edge case, implemented that recommendation immediately: parse_command/segment_subcommand now compare whole tokens exactly (never substring/regex matching), which structurally eliminates the entire bug class -- verified against every case raised across all 3 rounds (18 cases) plus new ones (newline-separated genuine compound, no-space-separator compound), all correct. Also added a SCAN_TIME_BUDGET_SECONDS aggregate circuit breaker (the per-line length cap alone didn't bound total time across many adversarial lines -- reviewer measured ~18s aggregate; reproduced and reduced to ~2s). Re-measured coverage on the full rewrite: 100%.

Fourth security re-review (stress-testing the round-3 tokenizer rewrite) found 2 blockers and 3 minors, all in the token-classification tables the reviewer itself called "a strictly better place for gaps to live" than regex tuning. Blocker 1: GIT_FLAGS_WITH_VALUE only listed -C/-c; every other global git flag that consumes a following argument (--git-dir, --work-tree, --namespace, --exec-path, --super-prefix, --attr-source) caused segment_subcommand to return the flag's VALUE as the subcommand, fully bypassing the gate -- reproduced end-to-end with a real staged secret ('git --git-dir .git commit -am msg' was allowed) before fixing by expanding the set. Blocker 2: the claimed 100% coverage did not reproduce from test/run-tests.sh -- the earlier measurement's driver script had exercised extra manual scenarios never codified as formal assertions (true touched-line coverage was 89.8%, matching the reviewer's own instrumentation). Fixed by re-measuring with a driver that runs nothing but `bash test/run-tests.sh` itself, which surfaced 2 more genuine gaps beyond what the reviewer named (find_style_violation's clean-completion path; style_gate_enabled's except branch, unreachable through the existing corrupt-harness.json test because that fixture's staged content also has a secret, so find_secret always returns first) -- closed both with 2 new tests, arriving at a genuinely reproducible 100%. Minor 1: segment_subcommand required the bare literal token "git", missing /usr/bin/git and paren-wrapped (git ...; fixed via is_git_token()'s os.path.basename check, explicitly NOT extended to sudo/env wrapper prefixes since that would require an open-ended wrapper-command allowlist inconsistent with the finite, enumerable flag/token classification approach -- documented as an accepted residual hole instead. Minor 2: has_staging_flag scanned every character of an attached short-flag cluster for a/i, wrongly denying -mfix, -Fdraft.txt, -S<hash> -m x, and anything after -- (a pathspec, not a flag); fixed with a VALUE_TAKING_SHORT_FLAGS stop-set and a break on a literal -- token. Minor 3 (heredoc/continuation quote-stripping gaps): documented in the header per the reviewer's own recommendation, not coded around. Mutation-tested all three security-critical fixes (GIT_FLAGS_WITH_VALUE, is_git_token, has_staging_flag) by reverting each to its pre-fix form and confirming the new regression tests fail, then restoring -- all three correctly caught their regression, none were tautological. Full suite: 431/431, zero regressions.

Fifth security re-review independently re-probed the round-4 fix rather than trusting it, and found Blocker 1 was NOT actually closed: the round-4 GIT_FLAGS_WITH_VALUE expansion was assembled from memory, not probed, and both missed 2 real value-taking global flags (--config-env, --shallow-file -- confirmed end-to-end with a real staged secret and an actual git 2.52 commit) and kept 2 that don't consume a following argument at all (--exec-path prints and exits; --super-prefix was removed in 2.52). Fixed by mechanically probing every long-option-shaped string in the git binary plus all 52 single-letter short flags (git <flag> ARG1VAL ZZBOGUS, classified by which token git calls the unknown subcommand) and using that probed set instead of a remembered one. Also found 2 more git-recognition gaps beyond is_git_token: \git (the standard idiom for bypassing a shell alias named git, not adversarial evasion -- fixed, one character) and { git ...; } (a brace group -- accepted as a documented residual hole per the reviewer's own call, same class as the sudo/env wrapper gap). Also found the continuation-hole documentation was wrong in both content and direction: it blamed quote-stripping and described only a false-denial outcome, when the actual mechanism is command_segments splitting on a literal newline without joining backslash-newline continuations first, and the real-world consequence demonstrated end-to-end is a fail-open bypass (a genuine 'git \\n commit' is not recognized as git-shaped at all, so the whole gate no-ops and the secret scan itself is skipped) -- corrected the header to state the right cause and both directions, weighted toward the more serious one. Independently re-measured coverage with the reviewer's own from-scratch shim (not trusting my numbers): 175/175, matching my own re-measurement exactly. Improved the attached-short-flag-cluster tests per the reviewer's suggestion to stage a real secret and assert a secret-assignment denial rather than just 'not denied', proving each command is recognized-as-commit and scanned, not merely unrecognized. Mutation-tested both security-critical fixes (the corrected GIT_FLAGS_WITH_VALUE set, the \git backslash-stripping in is_git_token) by reverting each and confirming the new regression tests fail, then restoring. Full suite: 445/445, zero regressions.

Round 5's reviewer, after independently re-verifying the round-5 fixes and confirming APPROVE (445/445, 175/175 coverage matching my own measurement exactly), sent a follow-up recommendation on the accepted backslash-newline-continuation hole: the header justified accepting it with 'joining continuations correctly requires real shell parsing', but the reviewer tested that claim on a scratch copy and disproved it for the unquoted case -- `command.replace('\\\n', ' ')` before quote-stripping closes the fail-open bypass (a continued 'git \\n commit' no longer no-ops the whole gate) at zero cost, with no new false positives (a continuation inside a quoted commit message still collapses to whitespace and gets stripped either way; a genuine compound command split across a continuation still denies). Applied the one-line fix, reworded the header to describe what's actually closed (unquoted case) versus what's still open (a continuation inside a heredoc body, which does need real state-tracking, not a one-line fix), added 3 regression tests (the bypass itself; the quoted-continuation false-positive check; the still-must-deny genuine-compound-across-a-continuation check), and mutation-tested the fix (reverted, confirmed the new test fails, restored). Full suite: 452/452, coverage still 100% (175/175).

Sixth security re-review independently re-verified GIT_FLAGS_WITH_VALUE and coverage rather than trusting either (both confirmed correct: 8-flag set matches git.c's handle_options() at v2.52.0 exactly; 175/175 lines, matching my own number), then found 2 new blockers and 1 major finding via differential fuzzing against a logging git shim. Blocker 1: command_segments never split on '&' (background execution, and the leading half of '|&'), so everything before it stayed glued to everything after it and only the first segment's subcommand was ever seen -- verified as a real, working commit path end-to-end, both for Check 1 (secret scan skipped) and Check 0 (a compound git-add-then-commit glued to an unrelated command via '&' produced no compound-stage-and-commit denial). Fixed by adding '&' to the split character class (one character; '&&' still matches its own earlier alternative first, so it isn't mistaken for two lone '&' separators). Blocker 2: the round-5 continuation-join fix (command.replace with no parity check) introduced its OWN fail-open regression -- an ESCAPED backslash (an even run) immediately before a genuine separator newline was wrongly joined into a continuation, hiding the second command from the gate entirely; the round-5 commit's own claim that 'no other matrix entry changes' was therefore false, with no test to catch it. Fixed by rewriting join_continuations to check backslash-run parity (odd -> real continuation, join; even -> real separator, leave the newline for command_segments). Major finding 3: segment_subcommand only skipped VAR=value env-assignment prefixes, so a shell reserved word leading a simple command inside a control structure (if/then, for/do, while/do, until/do) defeated recognition entirely -- unlike the sudo/env wrapper gap, this is a closed 4-word set, so it was enumerated and fixed (SHELL_LEADING_KEYWORDS) rather than merely documented; a 'case ... in PATTERN)' segment remains a documented residual hole since the token before git there is an arbitrary case pattern, not a fixed word. Also corrected 2 documentation overclaims (the header's 'a token from one logical command can never pair with a token from another' was falsified by blocker 1; the --super-prefix drop's narrow old-git-version regression wasn't called out) and 3 test-quality issues: raised 2 flaky wall-clock bounds that included process/subprocess startup overhead (1.0s->5.0s, 5.0s->15.0s), strengthened a clean-index 'not denied' assertion that couldn't distinguish 'recognized and clean' from 'unrecognized entirely' (the exact weakness that hid the continuation bypass) into a staged-secret positive-denial assertion, and added a secret-assignment content assertion to the per-flag test loop. Mutation-tested all three new fixes (the '&' separator, the parity-aware continuation join, the reserved-word skip) by reverting each and confirming its regression tests fail, then restoring. Full suite: 480/480, coverage 100% (185/185, up from 175 with the new join_continuations function and keyword set).

features.notes: Linear: OVI-54. Full spec (incl. Amendment) re-verified per-issue by /harness-issue-prep before implementation. Implemented as: (1) hooks/session-start.sh prints the session_id from its stdin payload as `Session: <id>` so the lead has a stable name for its mld filename, without ever referencing .harness/mld/ itself; (2) hooks/session-end.sh adds an informational (non-blocking) discipline note when no .harness/mld/<today>-*.md exists, mirroring the existing proof-note pattern rather than the hard-blocking Meta-Session gap, since the spec only calls the session-start non-read guarantee "hard" -- the write step is a softer, reviewed-on-its-own-cadence discipline; (3) skills/harness-continue/SKILL.md documents the MLD write step (lead-only) in both Step 5a (single-session) and Phase 5.5 (Agent Teams) Session End procedures; (4) rules/mld-review.md (new) defines the review cadence and four-way disposition (promote/escalate/action/discard) plus the commit-by-default note; (5) rules/task-completion.md gets a matching checklist item. The "hard" non-injection guarantee is enforced two ways: F006's pre-existing doctor.py check_mld_non_injection already static-greps the plugin's session-start.sh for the literal substring "mld" (built ahead of this feature); this feature adds (a) a permanent regression test asserting the real shipped session-start.sh source never contains that substring, and (b) a dynamic test running the real hook across all 4 SessionStart matcher sources (startup/resume/clear/compact, per hooks/hooks.json) with .harness/mld/ populated with a marker file, asserting the marker never leaks into stdout under any of them. Both were mutation-tested: (a) reverting the session_id print and forcing the discipline-note's MLD_FOUND flag true each failed only their own targeted assertions; (b) editing a throwaway copy of session-start.sh to `cat` .harness/mld/*.md caused all 4 dynamic-source assertions plus the static regression test to fail together, confirming both catch a real non-injection regression. Not touched (out of scope per the verified spec): README.md's project directory tree doesn't yet list .harness/mld/ as a scaffolded entry -- left as a documentation follow-up rather than expanding this feature's scope. ROUND 2 (adversarial review of PR #62): found session_id -- externally supplied, echoed unsanitized into the orientation block -- was a genuine injection vector on two axes: a newline injected arbitrary lines directly under the orientation header (the most authoritative position in this hook's output, indistinguishable from harness-authored content), and a "/"/".." let it escape its intended telemetry directory once the lead used it verbatim in a later filename. Fixed with one sanitization line (tr -cd to a safe charset, length-capped) that closes both at once; mutation-tested (removing it fails exactly the 2 security-relevant assertions). Also fixed: an explicit JSON `session_id: null` printed the literal string "None" (Python's .get(k, default) doesn't apply the default when the key exists with value null) -- changed to `.get(k) or ""`. session-end.sh's discipline note pointed at "rules/mld-review.md for the write step", which was both circular (that file defers back to harness-continue) and a bare-relative path that doesn't resolve in a user's project (rules/ ships with the plugin) -- repointed at /harness-continue's Session End step directly. My own first attempt at documenting the session_id sanitization fix violated the exact non-injection invariant it was fixing (the comment explaining the fix contained the literal lowercase substring the doctor.py check scans for) -- caught immediately by the new mldsrc regression test, which is exactly what it's for; fixed by keeping the directory unnamed in session-start.sh and adding a one-line pointer in the file header instead. "Append" was corrected to "Write" in two places (SKILL.md, and this feature's own description's spirit) since the file is one-per-session, not accumulated into. Disclosed scope boundary, unchanged from round 1 plus one addition: neither harness-init's scaffolding nor README.md's directory tree create/list .harness/mld/ -- consequence is that /harness-doctor's non-injection check is inert (returns no finding either way) until a project's FIRST mld file exists, since the check short-circuits on a missing directory; the dynamic and static tests in test/run-tests.sh cover the shipped plugin unconditionally regardless, so the guarantee itself still holds -- this is a left-out scaffolding step, not a gap in the guarantee's enforcement.
approaches_tried: Considered having the SessionEnd hook itself author the MLD file content -- rejected: SessionEnd fires when the session actually terminates, after the model's last turn, so it cannot produce reflective prose; the lead must write it during the conversation (mirroring how the Meta-Session retrospective is lead-authored into context_summary.md, with the hook only auditing presence).

Considered making the missing-mld-entry note a hard SESSION_INCOMPLETE gap like the Meta-Session check -- rejected: the spec calls only the session-start non-read guarantee "hard"; MLD's own review cadence (rules/mld-review.md) is explicitly NOT per-session, so gating every session on it would be a heavier bar than the feature asked for.

Round 2 fixes (adversarial review of PR #62), mutation-tested: (1) session_id sanitized via tr -cd 'A-Za-z0-9._-' | cut -c1-64 right after extraction, closing both the newline-injection and path-traversal findings with one line; verified against the exact reported payloads (a newline-plus-fake-heading string, and "../../../../etc/passwd") plus a JSON-null session_id. (2) session_id extraction changed to `.get("session_id") or ""` so an explicit JSON null doesn't print the string "None". (3) session-end.sh's discipline note re-pointed from a circular, non-resolving "rules/mld-review.md" reference to "/harness-continue's Session End step". (4) Added assert_rc0 to the md3 test for consistency with md1/md2. (5) "Append" -> "Write" in SKILL.md (the file is one-per-session, not accumulated into).

features.description:
skills/harness-init/enforce-scope.sh.template's segments_of() (line ~142) splits commands on `\|\||&&|[|;]` -- missing a literal newline. commit-gate.sh.template hit exactly this bug in F011's round-3 review and fixed it (its split includes 
); enforce-scope.sh never did. CONFIRMED FAIL-OPEN: a two-line command with an out-of-scope write on line 1 and an in-scope write on line 2 collapses into one segment; redirect_target() returns only the LAST '>' match on that merged segment, so the in-scope write on line 2 masks the out-of-scope write on line 1 and the whole command is ALLOWED. Verified end-to-end against a real scope fixture (.claude/teammate-scope.txt = 'src/allowed/'): baseline out-of-scope write denies, baseline in-scope write allows, the ';'-separated case denies correctly, but 'echo x > src/forbidden/a.txt
echo y > src/allowed/ok.txt' (real newline, not ';') is wrongly ALLOWED. Note the bug is narrower than commit-gate's equivalent: '&' does NOT bypass enforce-scope (redirect_target regexes over the whole merged segment rather than depending on the segment's leading token), only the missing newline split does. Likely fix is the same shape as commit-gate's (add 
, probably & too for consistency), but this hook has its own heredoc handling (strip_heredoc_bodies) and its own test surface, so it needs a real review, not a copied one-liner.
features.coverage: n/a (shell suite, no coverage tooling; full_test 530/530 is the gate)
features.notes: Discovered by F011/OVI-64's round-6 reviewer while idle, via one grep for the same bug class it had just spent that round on, then verified with a real fixture before reporting -- not fixed there since it's a different, already-shipped hook, out of F011's scope. Explicitly flagged as its own issue rather than folded into PR #40.
approaches_tried: Fixed by mirroring commit-gate.sh's round-3 fix exactly: added a literal newline and '&' to segments_of()'s split character class (unchanged: '&&' is still matched by its own earlier alternative first, so it isn't mistaken for two lone '&' separators). Before implementing, independently verified the reporting reviewer's own characterization rather than trusting it: they reported '& does NOT bypass enforce-scope' based on a single-write-target test case (true & echo x > forbidden), which is correct for that shape but doesn't exercise the actual masking mechanism (redirect_target() returning only the LAST >/>> match on a merged segment). Built a real scope fixture and confirmed the masking bug DOES reproduce for '&' once a command has two write targets glued together ('echo bad > forbidden & echo good > allowed' was wrongly ALLOWED, identical to the already-confirmed newline case) -- so '&' needed the fix, not just the newline. Wrote regression tests first (TDD red phase: confirmed both new tests fail against the pre-fix code, plus confirmed the && and no-new-false-positive cases already passed, proving the tests aren't tautological), then applied the fix, then mutation-tested it (reverted, confirmed both new tests fail, restored). Full suite: 490/490 (up from 480), no regressions. Kept the fix narrow (only the separator set, matching commit-gate's equivalent fix) rather than adding quote-stripping or other compound-detection machinery commit-gate has -- this hook's header already documents 'compound commands, quoting, subshells' as accepted evadable-by-construction surface, and this fix doesn't change that posture, just closes one concrete masking bug within it.

Round 1 review (REQUEST CHANGES): the fix itself (verified end-to-end against a real scope fixture) correctly closed both masking bugs, including confirming the peer reviewer's own '&' characterization was incomplete (their single-write-target test case didn't exercise the masking mechanism) -- but found the fix introduced 2 new blockers of its own, exactly the F011 pattern repeating at smaller scale. Blocker 1: splitting on a literal newline without first joining backslash-newline continuations severed 'sed -i' across a continuation, silently ALLOWING an out-of-scope sed -i edit (verified: was DENY pre-fix, ALLOW post-fix). Blocker 2: the same continuation split created false positives for cp/mv/rm split across a continuation, all writing in-scope (denial named a garbage '\' path). Both fixed by porting commit-gate.sh.template's join_continuations() (with its backslash-parity handling) verbatim and applying it before segmenting. Blocker 3: adding '&' to the split without quote-stripping would deny sed's legitimate 's/foo/[&]/' whole-match idiom and any quoted-'&' filename -- fixed by porting strip_quotes() too. Mutation-tested both ported fixes independently (not just combined): removing only join_continuations breaks exactly the 3 continuation tests and nothing else; removing only strip_quotes breaks exactly the 2 quoted-'&' tests and nothing else -- confirming the two fixes are orthogonal and each is independently load-bearing. Also fixed a genuinely tautological test the reviewer caught: an assertion claiming '&&' is 'consumed as its own operator, not split into two lone &' could not fail, because unlike commit-gate.sh (where token position matters for subcommand recognition), this hook's redirect_target() scans the WHOLE segment for a write target regardless of position, so && and two adjacent lone '&' characters segment identically here (verified independently: deleting the '&&' alternative from the regex changed no test's pass/fail status). Simplified the split regex to just [|;\n&] (dropping the now-provably-redundant \|\| and && alternatives) and relabeled the test as a plain sanity check rather than a false claim of distinguishing coverage. Documented (not fixed, per scope discipline) the reviewer's separate 'pre-existing, not introduced here' finding (multi-target masking via rm/tee/sed -i with 2+ files; cp -t/mv -t) as F024. Full suite: 502/502 (up from 490), coverage n/a (shell suite, no coverage tooling).

Round 2 confirming pass independently re-verified all 6 round-1 fixes against 3 fixtures built from actual git commits (main/c799450/9ca0584) and confirmed them genuinely fixed, then found round 1's strip_quotes port was itself a critical regression: erasing quoted spans (rather than masking them) fed quote-erased text into TARGET EXTRACTION, not just segmentation. Since this hook (unlike commit-gate.sh, where quotes only ever wrap non-target text like a commit message) routinely has its write target itself quoted, erasing quotes erased the target entirely -- 6 of 8 write shapes (redirect, rm, rm -rf, tee, sed -i, both quote styles) silently ALLOWED once quoted, including the separate lead-owned state-file guard. Verified each repro end-to-end against a real fixture before fixing. Root cause: porting strip_quotes() from commit-gate.sh was 'not like-for-like' -- the same shape of mistake as round 1 (porting a change without its prerequisites), one layer up. Fixed by replacing deletion with same-length masking (mask_quotes(), placeholder chars that never match a separator): segment boundaries are found in the masked copy, but segments themselves are sliced from the ORIGINAL, still-quoted text, so write_target()/redirect_target() see the real target; a target is unquoted (unquote_token()) only AFTER extraction, never before. Verified all round-2 repros now correctly deny (or, for cp/mv, correctly name the destination rather than falling through to the source), plus a bonus fix to a genuinely pre-existing FP (a quoted in-scope path containing a real '&', e.g. R&D, previously denied because the quote characters were never stripped from the comparison). Independently re-verified the round-2 report's 'apostrophe-pairing hazard' finding (echo don't > forbidden; echo won't > allowed, reported as a new ALLOW-when-should-DENY case) against REAL bash rather than accepting it: bash's own single-quote parsing genuinely swallows everything between the first and second apostrophe as a literal string, so the reported command never actually writes to the 'forbidden' path at all in real execution (confirmed by running it and inspecting which files were created) -- the tool's new ALLOW is correct, and the OLD DENY was the actual false positive. Reported this correction back rather than implementing an unnecessary workaround. Mutation-tested the fix by reverting to the erasure-based design: all 16 new round-2 regression tests correctly fail. Full suite: 530/530 (up from 502), no regressions.

Round 3 (final) confirming pass: APPROVE. Independently re-verified the reviewer's own round-2 apostrophe-pairing claim against real bash and retracted it themselves (matching my earlier correction). All round-1/2 fixes reconfirmed holding (continuation, quoted-&, quote-erasure) via a fresh fixture rebuilt from HEAD. Independently mutation-tested the fix's 4 components (mask_quotes, unquote_token, join_continuations, and the slice-from-original-vs-masked design choice) rather than trusting my own mutation numbers -- confirmed each is load-bearing (every component fails at least 2 assertions when broken) and reproduced my exact 16-assertion erasure-regression count after correcting their own first (flawed) mutation attempt. Filed F026 (pre-existing '..' path-traversal gap, exposed under two more spellings by the quote-erasure fix) as a non-blocking follow-up. Suite: 530/530.

features.description: skills/harness-init/enforce-scope.sh.template's write_target()/redirect_target() only ever return the LAST write target found in a segment (a `>>?\s*(...)` regex match via findall()[-1], or the last flagless token for tee/cp/mv/rm/sed -i). A command with MULTIPLE real write targets in one segment is checked only against its last target: `rm src/forbidden/a.txt src/allowed/b.txt` (verified: both files really deleted, only the last is scope-checked), `tee file1 file2` or `sed -i` given two files (same masking), all wrongly ALLOWED when the first target is out-of-scope and the last is in-scope. Separately, `cp -t DIR src...`/`mv -t DIR src...` (GNU-only; not present on BSD/macOS cp) put the real destination in a flag argument, which write_target() doesn't look for at all -- an out-of-scope -t destination is never checked. Neither shape is compound/quoted/subshell/heredoc, so the header's existing evadable-by-construction disclaimer doesn't cover them; they're a distinct residual, now documented in the header but not fixed.
features.coverage: n/a (shell suite, no coverage tooling; full_test 627/627 is the gate)
features.notes: Discovered by F023's round-1 reviewer while adversarially probing the missing-separator fix; explicitly flagged as pre-existing and not introduced by that PR, so not fixed there. Fixing likely requires write_target() to return ALL targets in a segment (checking each against scope, not just the last), plus recognizing -t/--target-directory as a destination-bearing flag for cp/mv.
approaches_tried: Rewrote write_target()->write_targets() (plural) to return EVERY real write target in a segment rather than just one: redirect_targets() now returns all >/>> matches (not matches[-1]); rm/tee use all_flagless_tokens() (all non-flag tokens, not last_flagless_token()); cp_mv_targets() adds -t/--target-directory= recognition (destination is the flag's value, every OTHER flagless argument is a source, read not written) while falling back to the existing last-flagless-token behavior when neither form is present (cp/mv without -t only ever write to their destination argument, never their sources, so multi-target checking doesn't apply there); sed_inplace_targets() treats every flagless token AFTER the first as a file target (the first is the sed script/expression, not a file). main() now iterates every segment's every target instead of one. TDD: wrote 12 assertions first (3 multi-target-masking cases, 3 cp/mv -t recognition cases, 2 no-new-false-positive cases, 1 plain cp/mv destination-only regression check), confirmed all fail against the pre-fix code. Implementing the naive 'return all matches/tokens' version introduced 2 of its own regressions, caught by the EXISTING test suite, not new tests: (1) redirect_targets() matching every raw '>' in the segment text treated a '>' INSIDE a quoted string (echo "a => b" > file) as a second, fake redirect -- fixed by matching against a quote-MASKED copy (mask_quotes) to find real operator positions, then slicing the target text from the ORIGINAL segment at those same positions, so a legitimately quoted target's real text still comes through. (2) sed_inplace_targets() returning ALL flagless tokens wrongly included the sed SCRIPT argument itself as a 'target' -- fixed by skipping the first flagless token (documented residual: multiple -e expressions, whose own values are also flagless tokens, aren't specially recognized; only the common single-script form is covered). Removed the now-unused WRITE_COMMANDS constant. Mutation-tested all 3 fixes independently (multi-target rm/tee, cp/mv -t recognition, sed script-skip): each reverts to exactly its own expected failure set. Full suite: 591/591 (up from 566), no regressions.

Round 1 review (REQUEST CHANGES): the 6 originally-reported cases were genuinely fixed, but found 4 blockers, all the recurring pattern of a fix introducing a new bug in an untested dimension. Blocker 1-3, one root cause: the sed script-skip heuristic ('skip exactly one leading flagless token') broke on 3 real shapes -- the mandatory-backup-suffix BSD/macOS idiom (`sed -i '' 's/a/b/' file`, ordinary work on this repo's own darwin platform, was wrongly denied, misreading the real script as the file); multiple -e expressions (`sed -i -e '...' -e '...' file`, each -e's own value is itself a flagless token, wrongly denied); and long-form attached script flags (`--expression=`/`--file=`, where there is NO positional script token to skip at all, so the blind [1:] slice dropped the real, sole file argument, wrongly ALLOWING an out-of-scope write). Fixed by rewriting sed_inplace_targets to walk tokens one at a time (mirroring commit-gate.sh's segment_subcommand flag-walking loop): -e/-f/--expression/--file each explicitly consume their own value; a bare -i followed by an empty-quote token ('' or "") consumes that as the BSD suffix; only when NO explicit script-providing flag is present does the first remaining flagless token get treated as an implicit script. Blocker 4: write_targets() treated redirect-target extraction and command-type extraction (cp/mv/tee/rm/sed) as ALTERNATIVES (checking command-type targets only when the segment had no redirect at all) rather than collecting both, so a real write command with an unrelated trailing redirect (`tee out-of-scope > in-scope-log`) only ever had the redirect checked -- the exact F024 masking shape, across extractor categories instead of within one. Fixed by adding strip_redirects() (removes real >/>> clauses, mask-aware, before tokenizing for the command-type extractors) and collecting BOTH redirect targets and command-type targets unconditionally. Also fixed 2 non-blocking findings: cp_mv_targets() now recognizes the attached -tDIR form (not just space-separated -t DIR); 2 stale comments referencing renamed singular function names, and the header's FP-residual/multi-match documentation updated for accuracy. Filed F029 (a pre-existing '--' pathspec-separator gap the review found while stress-testing, confirmed unrelated to F024) rather than expanding scope further. TDD: wrote 11 new assertions first, confirmed all fail against the pre-round-1-fix code. Mutation-tested both major fixes (the sed rewrite, the extractor-union change) independently: each reverts to exactly its own expected failure set. Full suite: 613/613 (up from 591), no regressions.

Round 2 confirming pass: all round-1 fixes reconfirmed genuinely fixed against a fresh fixture, but found one new blocking regression, again the recurring pattern -- round 1's strip_redirects() regex (`>>?\s*[^\s<>|&;]+`) removed a redirect's operator and target but not a PRECEDING file-descriptor digit (`2>`, `1>`), leaving a stray digit token that the command extractors (which now always run, per round 1's own fix) misread as a real write target -- a fully in-scope command (`rm file 2> log`, `tee file 2>> log`, `cp a b 1> log`, `sed -i '' ... 2> log`) was wrongly denied naming the bare digit. Fixed by anchoring the digit match to a token boundary (`(?:^|(?<=\s))\d*>>?...`), so a real fd-prefix digit (its own complete token) is correctly consumed as part of the operator, while a real argument merely ENDING in a digit right before an unprefixed redirect (`file2> out`, matching real bash: `echo abc2> out` writes 'abc2', not 'abc') is not mistaken for one and truncated -- the reviewer explicitly cautioned against a naive `\d*>>?` prefix, which would have mangled that second case; verified both shapes correctly with real hook invocations. Documented (not fixed, per the review's own explicit framing) a narrower related residual: `sed -i '.bak' 's/a/b/' file` (a non-empty, separately-quoted backup suffix, as opposed to the common attached `-i.bak` or empty `-i ''` forms) is misread as the implicit script and denies in-scope work -- widening the empty-string check would reintroduce the GNU/BSD ambiguity the function exists to resolve. Filed F030 (pre-existing `2>/dev/null` denial, confirmed unrelated to F024, a real usability issue given how common that idiom is) per the review's explicit recommendation to file separately. TDD: 3 new assertions, confirmed 2 genuinely fail against the pre-round-2-fix code (the third exercises a case masked by the pre-existing, separately-filed F030 issue). Mutation-tested the fix: reverting to the unanchored regex reproduces both real failures. Full suite: 619/619 (up from 613), no regressions.

Round 3 confirming pass: all round-2 fd-digit repros reconfirmed fixed, but found round 2's fix over-anchored -- it anchored the ENTIRE match (`(?:^|(?<=\s))\d*>>?...`) to a token boundary, not just the optional digit run, so a BARE '>' with no fd prefix at all failed to match unless it was ALSO preceded by whitespace. A redirect glued directly onto a cp/mv destination with no separating space (`cp a b> log`, a real, working command per real bash) was never stripped at all, so cp/mv's destination detection fell through to the unstripped trailing text and picked the redirect's own (possibly in-scope) target instead of the real destination -- reintroducing F024's own masking bug a third time, in a third untested dimension. Fixed by anchoring ONLY the optional digit group (`(?:(?:^|(?<=\s))\d+)?>>?...`), keeping it a genuinely optional prefix rather than gating the whole match on it -- verified against the reviewer's exact 5-case matrix (`cp a b> log` -> 'cp a b', `rm file2> out` -> 'rm file2', `rm a 2> out` -> 'rm a', `rm 2 > out` -> 'rm 2' (a file literally named '2'), `rm 2> out` -> 'rm') by calling strip_redirects() directly, all 5 matching exactly. Also fixed 2 test-quality issues the review caught: one new assertion used /dev/null as the redirect target, which the separately-filed F030 issue denies BEFORE the digit logic is ever reached, making it tautological (rewrote to use an in-scope target so it can actually discriminate); another asserted on a WITH-SPACE case ('version2 2> ...') that doesn't exercise the digit-vs-trailing-argument ambiguity at all (rewrote to the no-space form, 'version2> ...', which is the actual discriminating shape). Added 3 new regression tests for the no-space cp/mv masking bug (2 denial cases, 1 no-false-positive case). Mutation-tested by reverting to the over-anchored regex: the 3 relevant new assertions correctly fail. Full suite: 626/626 (up from 619), no regressions.

Round 4 (final) confirming pass: APPROVE, the first round in this PR's chain where the fix introduced no new regression -- the negative result. All round-1/2/3 fixes reconfirmed holding simultaneously (both fd-digit hazards satisfied together, e.g. `rm src/parser/2 > src/parser/err.log`, a file literally named '2', still correct). One non-blocking test nit: the 'version2' no-space test used an all-in-scope target, which couldn't actually discriminate a truncating regex from a correct one (a naively truncated 'version' was still in scope right alongside the correct 'version2') -- switched to an out-of-scope target so the denial message's exact filename proves no truncation occurred; mutation-tested against the naive `\d*` regex to confirm the test now genuinely fails when truncation happens. Folded one more pre-existing finding into F030 (not this PR): `rm file 2>&1` denies naming the dangling '2>' fragment, confirmed unchanged across every round of this PR back to main. Full suite: 627/627 (up from 626), no regressions. PR #46 merged.

features.description: skills/harness-init/commit-gate.sh.template's strip_quotes() deletes quoted spans (replacing them with a single space) before parse_command() tokenizes the command to find its git subcommand. Since the secret scan itself reads the real staged git diff (staged_diff()), not the quote-stripped command string, Check 1 (secret-assignment/url-credential) is unaffected by this bug in isolation -- but subcommand DETECTION runs on the quote-stripped text, and quoting any part of the 'git'/'commit' tokens erases them before parse_command() ever sees a 'commit' subcommand. main() then returns before EITHER the compound-stage-and-commit check OR the secret scan run at all. CONFIRMED end-to-end with a real staged secret: `git commit -m x` correctly denies (secret-assignment); `git "commit" -m x` is silently ALLOWED with the identical staged secret -- one quote character around the word 'commit' disables the entire gate, including the secret scan it exists to run. Same confirmed for `git 'commit' -m x`, `"git" commit -m x`, and `git com"mit" -m x` (all real, working git-commit invocations per bash tokenization). Same root cause as F023's round-2 finding in a different hook (enforce-scope.sh.template): strip_quotes() deletes content that is load-bearing for the gate's decision -- there it erased the write target, here it erases the subcommand token. Lower severity than F023's case in one sense (needs someone to deliberately quote a command token, unusual, vs. quoting a path, which is the ordinary case) but higher in consequence (fully disables secret scanning, not just one masked target) and it is ALREADY SHIPPED, actively-relied-upon security infrastructure, not a pending PR.
features.coverage: n/a (shell suite, no coverage tooling; full_test 547/547 is the gate)
features.notes: Discovered by F023's round-1 reviewer while idle, verifying its own earlier claim that commit-gate.sh's strip_quotes() is safe (it isn't, for subcommand detection, though the secret scan itself is unaffected since it reads the real git diff, not the quote-stripped command string). Independently re-verified end-to-end with a real staged secret before filing. Elevated priority given it's a live bypass of already-shipped security infrastructure, not a pending change. Likely fix: the same mask-then-slice approach used to fix F023 in enforce-scope.sh.template -- segment on quote-masked text to find boundaries, but keep the ORIGINAL quoted text for subcommand token comparison, stripping only the quote characters (not content) from each token before comparing to 'git'/'commit'/flag names. Worth hoisting the shared mask/unquote helpers into one place if fixed the same way a third time, per the reviewer's own suggestion.
approaches_tried: Fixed with the same mask-then-slice design used to close F023's round-2 finding in enforce-scope.sh.template, adapted for this hook's TOKEN-based subcommand recognition rather than F023's whole-segment regex scan: mask_quotes() replaces each quoted span with same-length placeholder characters (never a real separator or token boundary), used only to find command_segments()'s split positions; segments themselves are sliced from the ORIGINAL, still-quoted text. Unlike F023, quotes aren't stripped once from a whole segment -- since is_git_token/segment_subcommand/has_staging_flag all compare individual TOKENS by exact string equality (against 'git', 'commit', GIT_FLAGS_WITH_VALUE, STAGING_FLAGS, etc.), each token is unquoted (unquote_token()) individually right after seg.split(), before any comparison runs -- so 'commit', 'commit', $'commit', and com"mit" (fully or partially quoted, any of the 3 quote styles) all normalize to the bare word 'commit' before comparison. Changed parse_command()/check_compound_stage_and_commit() to carry the already-tokenized-and-unquoted token list through 'parsed' instead of the raw segment text plus a re-split -- avoids a second, redundant tokenization pass and keeps unquoting in exactly one place. TDD: wrote 4 quoted-subcommand-token regression tests plus a quoted-staging-flag test first, confirmed all 9 assertions fail against the pre-fix code (red phase), implemented, confirmed green. Manually verified beyond the formal test cases: quoted global flags (--git-dir), a quoted VAR=value prefix, and a quoted SHELL_LEADING_KEYWORDS entry (then) all still correctly recognize a git-commit invocation and deny a real staged secret; a normal commit message merely mentioning the word 'commit' still denies for the right reason (secret-assignment), not a false compound match. Mutation-tested both the unquote_token application in parse_command and the mask-then-slice segmentation design independently -- reverting either reproduces exactly the original 9 red-phase failures. Full suite: 547/547, no regressions.

Round 1 review (REQUEST CHANGES): confirmed the bypass itself closed (all 6 quoted-token repros denied, verified against real bash/git that each is a genuine commit invocation), but found the fix introduced 2 new regressions with one shared root cause -- command_segments()'s mask-then-slice fix preserved quoted content at the SEGMENT level, but parse_command still tokenized with naive seg.split(), which treats whitespace INSIDE a quoted commit message as a real token boundary (a pre-existing weakness the old strip_quotes()-based design had accidentally masked, by deleting the message text those pseudo-tokens came from). Fail-open: a quoted '--' anywhere in a commit message shattered into its own pseudo-token, misread by has_staging_flag as the pathspec separator, stopping its scan before reaching a REAL trailing staging flag (`git commit -m "see --" -a` was wrongly ALLOWED, with a secret only in the unstaged working tree so the scan saw nothing). False positive: flag-shaped words inside a quoted message with no real staging flag anywhere ('fix: handle -a and -i staging flags') wrongly triggered a compound-stage-and-commit denial on a clean repo. Fixed with split_tokens(): the same mask-then-slice discipline applied one level deeper than command_segments() -- \S+ runs found in the masked copy (quoted whitespace no longer matches \S) but sliced from the original segment, so a quoted multi-word string stays one token. Fixed a tautological test the review caught: a 'no false positive' assertion on a fixture with a staged secret could not fail for its stated reason (any bug producing a deny, including a false compound match, would satisfy assert_deny_json equally) -- strengthened to assert secret-assignment specifically and not-compound. Also fixed 2 stale citations (unquote_token's comment cited 'PR #42/F025'; PR #42 is F023, F025's own PR is #44). Mutation-tested split_tokens() by reverting to naive seg.split(): all 10 new assertions correctly fail. Full suite: 566/566 (up from 547), no regressions.

Independently re-verified all round-1 fixes from scratch (not on trust) -- all 3 shadowed-flag and 8 false-positive repros correct, 566/566, the mutation test independently re-run with the same 10-assertion failure set, the tautology fix and citation corrections both exactly as recommended, scope discipline held (enforce-scope.sh.template correctly left untouched, matching round 1's own advisory framing). Independently re-checked the F023-round-2-style apostrophe-pairing risk against real bash and found it harmless (the one ALLOW case is a bash syntax error that can never execute). Explicitly recommended merging anyway -- closing a wide, live secret-scan bypass outweighs reopening one narrow pre-existing pinhole -- and amended F027 to cover all three shapes for the next session. features.description: skills/harness-init/enforce-scope.sh.template's normalize() strips the project-root prefix from a target path but never resolves '..' path traversal, so a write target that leaves an allowed directory via traversal still matches the allowed prefix via a bare .startswith() check. CONFIRMED: with scope 'src/allowed/', `echo x > src/allowed/../forbidden/x.txt` writes to src/forbidden/x.txt in real bash (verified) but was ALLOWED even before F023 (pre-existing on main, not introduced by F023/PR #42). unquote_token (added to fix F023's round-2 quote-erasure bug) means two MORE spellings now reach the same pre-existing gap: `echo x > "src/allowed/"../forbidden/x.txt` and `echo x > "src/allowed/../forbidden/x.txt"` were incidentally denied on main (only because the un-stripped quote characters broke the .startswith() match, not because traversal was detected), and now reach the same ALLOW as the unquoted form once quotes are correctly stripped from the extracted target. Same family as F024 (multi-target masking) and F025 (commit-gate.sh quoted-token erasure) -- rated above F024 in severity since '..' is the classic scope-escape primitive and needs no multi-target trick, just an ordinary-looking relative path.
features.coverage: n/a (shell suite, no coverage tooling; full_test 649/649 is the gate)
features.notes: Discovered by F023's round-3 (final) reviewer while confirming the quote-erasure fix; explicitly framed as pre-existing on main (not a regression from F023/PR #42) and not a blocker to that PR's approval. Likely fix: normalize() should resolve '..'/'.' segments (e.g. via os.path.normpath on the target joined to project_root, then re-deriving the relative path) before the scope-prefix comparison, so a traversal that escapes the allowed directory is caught regardless of how the path was spelled or quoted.
approaches_tried: Fixed normalize() to resolve '.'/'..' segments via os.path.normpath after stripping the project-root prefix, so a write target that escapes an allowed directory via traversal no longer merely STARTS WITH the allowed prefix string -- both the scope-prefix check and the lead-owned exact-match check read the same normalize() output, so one fix closes both. A path resolving outside the project entirely (more '..' than real leading segments) is left with a leading '..' by normpath, which correctly never matches any scope pattern, so no special-case handling was needed for that case. Implementing the naive fix (bare os.path.normpath, nothing else) introduced its own regression, caught by 3 EXISTING (pre-F026) tests, not new ones: normpath strips a trailing '/', which this hook's directory-style scope patterns and a `cp -t DIR/` destination rely on for exact-directory-match comparisons -- an in-scope `cp -t src/parser/ ...` (destination IS the scope directory itself) was wrongly denied once the trailing slash disappeared. Fixed by restoring a trailing slash when the pre-normalize path had one. TDD: wrote 6 new test cases (13 assertions) first (3 denial cases: unquoted/quoted-prefix/fully-quoted traversal, identical scope-escape target; 2 no-false-positive cases: a traversal that resolves back in-scope, a redundant './'; 1 traversal into a lead-owned file), confirmed all 5 discriminating ones fail against the pre-fix code (the resolves-in-scope case already passed, since it doesn't involve any bug). Mutation-tested both the traversal-resolution fix and the trailing-slash preservation fix independently -- each reverts to exactly its own expected failure set (5 assertions for traversal-resolution, the 3 pre-existing cp -t assertions for trailing-slash). Full suite: 640/640 (up from 627), no regressions.

Round 1 review (REQUEST CHANGES): the Python-side normalize() fix verified correct via an independent fuzz sweep (286 generated traversal paths, 45 genuine bypasses on main -> 0 after the fix; 33-command non-traversal corpus, zero verdict changes) and mutation-tested cleanly, but found the IDENTICAL bug still live in the Edit/Write/MultiEdit legacy path (FILE_PATH, handled entirely in bash before normalize() is ever reached) -- the MORE authoritative gate, since Edit/Write is blocked outright while Bash coverage is only best-effort. Confirmed end-to-end: a teammate scoped to 'src/parser/' could Edit 'src/parser/../other/y.py' (escapes scope) or 'src/parser/../../.harness/features.json' (a lead-owned file) with both wrongly ALLOWED, directly defeating F009's stated acceptance language that lead-owned files are denied 'regardless of scope patterns'. Fixed by routing FILE_PATH through the same prefix-strip-then-normpath-then-restore-trailing-slash resolution as normalize(), removing the now-redundant bare bash-side prefix stripping. Verified against the reviewer's exact reported cases plus an additional one they didn't test (traversal past the project root entirely, e.g. '../../../etc/passwd', now correctly blocked instead of silently allowed). Also: strengthened the 2 quoted-traversal tests to assert the resolved path specifically (not just any deny), per the review's non-blocking finding that a fully-broken unquote_token could otherwise still deny for the wrong reason and the assertion wouldn't notice; documented (not fixed) two further residuals the review found -- normpath's purely lexical resolution can't see a symlink that would make real bash land somewhere different (not a regression, no traversal resolution existed at all before F026), and a backslash-escaped traversal segment (`\..`) still bypasses since unquote_token only strips quote characters, never shell backslash-escapes -- filed as F031, independently re-verified against real bash before filing. TDD: 4 new assertions for the Edit-path fix, confirmed failing against the pre-fix code. Mutation-tested the Edit-path fix independently: reverting it reproduces exactly the same 4 failures. Full suite: 648/648 (up from 640), no regressions.

Round 2 (final) confirming pass: APPROVE, a genuine negative result on the security axis (a 460-case fuzz sweep of the Edit/Write path found 67 genuine bypasses at the pre-round-1-fix commit, 0 after). Independently mutation-tested the `if path:` empty-file_path guard (127 assertions fail without it, confirming it's thoroughly load-bearing -- without it, os.path.normpath('') returning '.' would make every Bash-only tool call misroute into the Edit branch). Found an unadvertised side-benefit of the fix: the OLD bash-side `${FILE_PATH#$PROJECT_ROOT/}` used unquoted $PROJECT_ROOT in glob-pattern position, so a project root containing a shell metacharacter (e.g. 'root[1]') broke it, wrongly blocking in-scope edits -- the new Python-side literal str.startswith() doesn't have this problem; added a dedicated regression test with a bracket-containing fixture path, mutation-tested against the old bash-side code to confirm it genuinely fails there. Also found the FILE_PATH trailing-slash-restore logic (copied from normalize() for symmetry) was dead code for this specific path -- an Edit/Write/MultiEdit file_path is always a file, never a directory, so there's no directory-style scope-pattern case to preserve; confirmed via mutation (removing it changed zero assertions) and removed it rather than test genuinely unreachable code, per this project's 'no error handling for impossible states' standard. Added a one-line pointer in the file's residual-hole header index to the symlink-lexical-resolution and backslash-escape (F031) limitations, both already fully documented in normalize()'s own comment but not previously visible from the header's own residual list. Fixed a metadata wording nit (this entry claimed '6 new assertions' when it was actually 6 test cases spanning 13 assertions). Full suite: 649/649 (up from 648, +1 for the glob-metacharacter regression test), no regressions. PR #48 merged.

features.description: skills/harness-init/commit-gate.sh.template's has_staging_flag() does not distinguish a bare '--' token that is the ARGUMENT VALUE of a preceding space-separated value-taking short flag (e.g. `-m --`) from a real '--' pathspec separator. VALUE_TAKING_SHORT_FLAGS only handles the ATTACHED-value form (`-mfix`, one token); a space-separated value (`-m`, `--` as two tokens) is not recognized as belonging to `-m` at all, so has_staging_flag's per-token loop treats the following '--' as if it were a real pathspec separator and stops scanning -- missing a REAL staging flag later in the same segment. This is the general root cause; it surfaces in 3 related but distinct shapes, ALL false-positive/false-negative errors caused by the SAME missing behavior (has_staging_flag not knowing that -m's space-separated value is a value, not a token to interpret): (1) PRE-EXISTING, unaffected by F025: `git commit -m -- -a` (no quoting at all) is wrongly ALLOWED on main and on F025's fix alike, even though -a is a real, working staging flag -- a FALSE NEGATIVE, since this command genuinely does stage and commit in one step. (2) NARROWED BY F025 (round-2 review, not a wide bypass, one specific input shape): `git commit -m "--" -a` -- a quoted commit message whose ENTIRE content is exactly '--' -- was correctly DENIED on main (the old strip_quotes design deleted the quoted content, so has_staging_flag never saw a '--' pseudo-token there at all and reached the real trailing -a) but is wrongly ALLOWED after F025's fix -- also a FALSE NEGATIVE, same as shape (1): -a is a real staging flag here too. (3) NEW FALSE POSITIVE introduced by F025 (round-2 correction: the initial filing of this shape had the polarity backwards -- corrected here): `git commit -m "-a"` / "-i" / "--all" / "--include" -- a quoted commit message whose ENTIRE content is exactly a staging-flag string -- is wrongly DENIED as compound-stage-and-commit after F025's fix. VERIFIED against real git: this command stages nothing extra -- `-a` becomes the commit message text (log subject '-a'), only already-staged content is committed, and an unstaged working-tree edit plus an untracked file both survive untouched. main correctly ALLOWED this (an ordinary commit of already-staged content, not a stage-and-commit-in-one-step operation); F025's fix wrongly denies it because split_tokens()/unquote_token() reduce the quoted message to exactly the string '-a', indistinguishable from a real flag by has_staging_flag's exact-token comparison. This is a REGRESSION versus main, not an improvement -- the fix for shapes (1)/(2) must not special-case this shape to preserve the current (wrong) DENY; the correct fix makes it ALLOW again, matching main. All three shapes require the ENTIRE quoted message to be exactly a flag token or '--' with nothing else in it; the common case (flag-shaped words among other words, e.g. "fix: handle -a and -i staging flags") is already correct in both directions after F025 and is not part of this ticket.
features.coverage: n/a (shell suite, no coverage tooling; full_test is the gate)
features.notes: Discovered by F025's round-1 reviewer while verifying the quoted-'--' regression fix; confirmed pre-existing (case 1) on main. Round 2 found cases 2 and 3 on the same root cause. No Linear issue (internal, same precedent as F022-F026). Adversarial review of PR #49 round 1 found the initial fix's `len(tok) == 2` guard missed multi-letter short-flag clusters ending on a value-taking flag (e.g. '-sm'), not just a bare 2-char token -- fixed by making _scan_short_flag_cluster position-aware (value-taking flag must be the LAST char in the cluster) instead of guarding on token length. Round 2 then found that fix itself wrongly applied the position-aware bare-value-consumption rule to -S and -u, which real git parses as optargs (PARSE_OPT_OPTARG): a BARE -S/-u does NOT consume the next token, unlike -m/-F/-t/-C/-c. Split VALUE_TAKING_SHORT_FLAGS (all 7 letters, for recognizing an ATTACHED value like -uall/-Skeyid so it isn't misread as further flag letters) from REQUIRED_VALUE_SHORT_FLAGS (mFtCc only, for the bare/next-token-consuming case). Scoped to SHORT flags only; the identical gap for LONG flags (--message, --file, etc.) is pre-existing on main and filed separately as F032, not folded into this fix, to keep this PR's diff focused on what it already covers.
approaches_tried: Traced all 3 shapes by hand against has_staging_flag()'s token loop before writing any fix, confirming the unifying root cause matched the feature's own filed diagnosis: the loop never recognized that a bare (unattached) value-taking short flag's NEXT token is opaque value data, not something to interpret as a flag or the '--' separator. Rewrote the loop as index-based (while + manual i+=1) so it can skip exactly one token after such a flag.

Extracted _scan_short_flag_cluster() as a small helper returning (is_staging_flag, took_bare_value) to keep has_staging_flag's own cyclomatic complexity comfortably under this project's hard limit of 8, rather than risk a borderline count in a single larger function.

Round 2 (adversarial review of PR #49): the round-1 fix's position-aware took_bare_value applied uniformly to all 7 letters in VALUE_TAKING_SHORT_FLAGS, but real git's -S/-u are optargs whose BARE form does not consume the next token (confirmed against git 2.52.0: `git commit -u -a -m x` and `git commit -S -a -m x` both genuinely stage and commit, matching plain no-value flags like -n/-s, not -m/-F/-t/-C/-c). Split out REQUIRED_VALUE_SHORT_FLAGS (mFtCc) as the subset that also consumes a bare/next-token value; -S/-u stay in VALUE_TAKING_SHORT_FLAGS only for their attached-value form. Mutation-tested by reverting to the round-1 (non-split) version: exactly the 4 new -S/-u regression tests fail, confirming they catch it; restored and re-verified 670/670 green.

features.description: skills/harness-init/enforce-scope.sh.template's redirect_target() regex (`>>?\s*([^\s<>|&;]+)`) truncates a quoted path at its first internal space, since the character class stops at whitespace regardless of quote context and the segment isn't tokenized with a quote-aware splitter (the way commit-gate.sh.template's split_tokens(), added in F025, is). CONFIRMED: `echo x > "my file.txt"` extracts target 'my', not the real path. NOT currently exploitable: the truncated value keeps its directory prefix, so the scope check (`norm.startswith(p)`, a directory-prefix pattern) reaches the same verdict as the full path would; the one place an exact-match check exists (`norm in LEAD_OWNED`) compares against a fixed 3-path set, none of which contains a space, so no reachable bypass exists today. A latent robustness gap that would become a real fail-open only if a lead-owned path containing a space were ever added. CORRECTION (round-2 review of PR #51): this 'not currently exploitable' claim was WRONG for the second root cause named earlier in this same description (the missing quote-aware tokenizer) -- true only for the single-target redirect path that F024 incidentally closed. write_targets()'s own command_tokens extraction used a plain `.split()`, which shatters a quoted target containing a space into two pseudo-tokens BEFORE cp/mv/rm/sed-i extraction runs. This produced a reachable fail-open: `cp a.txt "src/other/evil src/parser/ok.txt"` was wrongly ALLOWED, since cp/mv's last-flagless-token destination logic picked only the in-scope-looking tail fragment, never seeing the real (out-of-scope) whole path. It also produced a non-adversarial false deny (`rm "src/parser/my file.txt"` denied naming a path -- 'file.txt' -- the user never typed).
features.coverage: n/a (shell suite, no coverage tooling; full_test 692/692 is the gate)
features.notes: Discovered by F025's reviewer during idle time, checking whether F025's token-level root cause (naive whitespace splitting inside quoted content) also affects the sibling hook. Explicitly assessed as low-priority, not exploitable today, and out of scope for F025's PR (a different hook). Likely fix: a quote-aware tokenizer shared with commit-gate.sh's split_tokens()/mask_quotes()/unquote_token() -- the reviewer notes this would be the third independent implementation of the same mask-then-slice pattern across these two hooks (F023's enforce-scope fix, F025's commit-gate fix, and this one), worth hoisting into one shared place if fixed, per F025's own approaches_tried notes on the same point. RESOLVED AS A SIDE EFFECT OF F024: by the time this feature was picked up, F024's mask_quotes()-based redirect_targets() rewrite had already landed and closed this gap incidentally (the NUL-masked quoted span contains no real whitespace, so the character class no longer stops mid-quote). No code change was needed; 2 regression tests were added instead to lock the correct behavior in. ROUND 2 (adversarial review of PR #51): confirmed the redirect_target() half was genuinely resolved by F024, but the write_targets() naive .split() half named in this feature's own 'Likely fix' note was still live -- a reachable scope-bypass fail-open (cp/mv) plus a false-deny (rm), not just a cosmetic gap. Fixed by adding split_tokens() (ported from commit-gate.sh.template's own split_tokens(), the third independent implementation of the same mask-then-slice pattern this feature's own notes already flagged as worth hoisting) and routing command_tokens through it instead of a bare .split(). Mutation-tested: reverting to the bare .split() fails exactly the 5 new round-2 assertions, including the genuine cp/mv fail-open (denial disappears entirely, not just misnamed) and the sed mangled-name case.
approaches_tried: Confirmed the bug as originally filed (naive char-class regex truncating a quoted target at its first internal space) no longer reproduces on current main: F024 (merged after this feature was filed) rewrote redirect_target() into redirect_targets(), matching against a mask_quotes() copy where a quoted span -- space included -- is replaced by a same-length NUL run, so the whitespace-stopping character class never sees a real space inside quotes. Verified directly by re-deriving the exact live functions and tracing echo x > "my file.txt" end to end: the full quoted span is captured, then unquote_token() strips the quote chars, yielding the untruncated target.

Added 2 regression tests locking in the correct behavior (out-of-scope quoted-space target denied and named in full; in-scope quoted-space target allowed) rather than changing any code, since no reproducible bug remains to fix.

Round 2: ported commit-gate.sh.template's split_tokens() (mask_quotes()-based, same mask-then-slice discipline as this file's own segments_of()/redirect_targets()) into enforce-scope.sh.template, and changed write_targets() to route strip_redirects(segment) through it instead of Python's bare .split(). Verified the genuine fail-open (cp/mv picking an in-scope-looking tail fragment as 'the' destination, never seeing the real out-of-scope whole path) by hand-tracing the old code, then confirmed the fix by mutation-testing: reverting to the bare .split() reproduces both the false deny and the fail-open, restoring the fix fixes both.

features.description: skills/harness-init/enforce-scope.sh.template's all_flagless_tokens() (used by rm/tee target extraction and cp_mv_targets()' fallback) treats any token starting with '-' as a flag, unconditionally, with no awareness of '--' as the POSIX pathspec separator. A real command like `rm -- -a.txt` (where -a.txt is a literal filename, not a flag, because -- ends flag parsing) is misread: '--' and '-a.txt' are BOTH excluded as flag-shaped, so no target is identified at all and the command is wrongly ALLOWED even when -a.txt is out of scope. Sibling hook commit-gate.sh.template handles this exact shape explicitly (has_staging_flag's `if tok == "--": break` plus its own test case for `git commit -- -a.txt`) -- this hook never got the equivalent treatment. Pre-existing, not introduced by F024; confirmed still present after F024's rewrite.
features.coverage: n/a (shell suite, no coverage tooling; full_test 724/724 is the gate)
features.notes: Discovered by F024's round-1 reviewer while stress-testing the all_flagless_tokens()/cp_mv_targets() rewrite; explicitly confirmed pre-existing (not introduced by F024) and out of scope for that PR. Likely fix: recognize a literal '--' token as ending flag parsing for the rest of a segment's tokens (every subsequent token is a pathspec, never a flag, even if it starts with '-'), mirroring commit-gate.sh.template's has_staging_flag(). Fixed by making all_flagless_tokens() --aware and rewriting last_flagless_token() as a thin wrapper over it, eliminating the duplicate flag-detection logic the two functions previously carried independently. ROUND 2 (adversarial review of PR #52): all_flagless_tokens() was fixed, but cp_mv_targets()'s own -t/--target-directory= scan had the identical '--' gap (a different function, same bug class) -- a literal filename starting with '-t' placed after '--' was misread as the -t flag and string-sliced into a bogus target, letting the real (possibly out-of-scope) destination go unchecked. sed_inplace_targets() had the same gap too. Both fixed: cp_mv_targets() now breaks its -t scan at a literal '--' (falling through to the already-fixed last_flagless_token() for the real destination); sed_inplace_targets() now stops all flag-detection once '--' is seen, letting every later token fall through to its ordinary implicit-script-then-target logic. Also fixed: features.json's lost trailing newline. ROUND 3 (adversarial review of PR #52): round 2's sed_inplace_targets() fix only made the token-walking LOOP '--'-aware; two any()-based guards ABOVE the loop (the -i/--in-place presence check, and has_explicit_script) still scanned the FULL argument list, including tokens after '--'. This caused both a false deny (a real out-of-scope file merely starting with '-i', e.g. `sed 's/a/b/' -- -input.txt`, with no actual -i flag anywhere, wrongly treated as an in-place edit) and a misnamed denial (`sed -i 's/a/b/' -- -e`, a real file literally named '-e', wrongly triggered has_explicit_script and got the SCRIPT text denied instead of the real file). Fixed by computing both guards over args truncated at the first '--' (pre_separator_args) instead of the full args list. Also swapped the round-2 second-'--' test for a discriminating one: the trailing '--' is now itself the target being tested (`rm -- src/parser/a.txt --`), since the original two-real-targets version passed identically whether or not a second '--' was treated as literal text. ROUND 4 (adversarial review of PR #52): round 3's pre_separator_args used a naive args.index('--'), but the token-walking loop uses a flag-aware walk that skips a '--' consumed as an -e/-f/--expression/--file VALUE (a script file literally named '--', e.g. `sed -f -- 's/a/b/'`). The two could disagree, truncating the guards one token early and missing a genuine -i flag positioned right after the value-consumed '--' -- a false negative (`sed -f -- -i src/other/f.txt` wrongly ALLOWED an in-place edit of an out-of-scope file). Fixed by extracting _separator_index(args), duplicating the loop's own flag-aware walk as a plain boundary lookup, and using it for both the guards and (implicitly, unchanged) the loop, so they always agree. Filed F037 for two unrelated, lower-severity, MORE-reachable gaps found in the same review: sed_inplace_targets() doesn't recognize clustered short flags (`-ri`, `-ni`) or the attached long-form suffix (`--in-place=.bak`) as specifying in-place mode at all -- a different bug class (flag recognition, not '--' awareness), deliberately not folded into this round's fix.
approaches_tried: Made all_flagless_tokens() the single source of truth for -- separator handling: the first literal "--" token ends flag parsing, every token after it is kept regardless of a leading "-" (mirrors commit-gate.sh.template has_staging_flag()'s "if tok == '--': break"). Rewrote last_flagless_token() as a one-line wrapper (flagless[-1] if flagless else None) instead of its own separate reversed-scan loop, removing a second, now-redundant implementation of the same flag-detection rule.

Mutation-tested by reverting to the pre-fix versions of both functions: the same 5 new assertions failed (and only those 5), confirming the tests actually catch the bug; restored and re-verified 659/659 green.

Round 2: added 'if tok == "--": break' to cp_mv_targets()'s own scan loop (falls through to last_flagless_token(), which already handles '--' correctly via the round-1 fix) and a past_separator flag to sed_inplace_targets() that disables all flag-detection once '--' is seen. Mutation-tested both independently: reverting cp_mv_targets()'s break fails exactly its own 4 new assertions; reverting sed_inplace_targets()'s past_separator gating fails exactly its own 2 new assertions (after correcting an initial non-discriminating test case that used a target not starting with '-', which passed under both old and new code since only dash-prefixed tokens were ever at risk).

Round 3: restricted sed_inplace_targets()'s two any()-based pre-checks to pre_separator_args (args[:args.index('--')] when '--' is present, else args unchanged), matching the token-walking loop's own '--'-awareness. Mutation-tested both new assertions independently by reverting to full-args scanning: each fails exactly its own assertion. Also mutation-tested the corrected trailing-'--' test against an 'every -- is a separator' mutant of all_flagless_tokens(): fails, confirming it (unlike its round-2 predecessor) actually discriminates.

Round 4: extracted _separator_index(args) (a flag-aware walk identical to the existing loop's, but as a pure boundary lookup with no side effects) and used it for pre_separator_args instead of a naive args.index('--'). Mutation-tested by reverting to the naive index: fails exactly the 2 new assertions for 'sed -f -- -i FILE'.

features.description: skills/harness-init/enforce-scope.sh.template denies any command containing a redirect to /dev/null (e.g. `cmd 2>/dev/null`, an extremely common idiom for discarding stderr) as an out-of-scope write, since /dev/null doesn't match any teammate scope pattern and there's no special-case exemption for it (unlike `.env.example`-style path exemptions used elsewhere in this repo's hooks). CONFIRMED PRE-EXISTING on main (not introduced by F024): `cp src/parser/a.txt src/parser/b.txt 2>/dev/null`, with every other real target in scope, is denied naming '/dev/null' on both main and after F024. A real usability problem: this idiom is common enough that it will likely trigger frequently in normal teammate work. A related, pre-existing shape (confirmed unchanged across every round of F024/PR #46, from main through the final merge): `rm <in-scope-file> 2>&1` is denied naming '2>' as the write target. Cause: segments_of() splits on a literal '&' (needed for other separator cases), which slices '2>&1' into 'rm <file> 2>' + '1' as two pieces of the same segment boundary set -- the dangling '2>' fragment has no target text after it for strip_redirects() to recognize as a real redirect, so nothing strips it, and it survives into the command tokens as a bogus flagless 'target'. Only affects cp/mv/tee/rm/sed (an unprefixed `> f 2>&1` is fine, since 'echo'/similar aren't in the command-type extractor set). `2>&1` is common enough (redirecting stderr to stdout) to be a real usability problem alongside `2>/dev/null`.
