features.notes: Discovered by F024's round-2 reviewer while verifying the fd-digit fix; explicitly confirmed pre-existing on main and unrelated to F024, recommended as a separate ticket rather than folding into that PR. Likely fix: exempt /dev/null (and possibly other /dev/* special files, e.g. /dev/stdout, /dev/stderr) from the scope check the same way *.env.example paths are already exempted, since writing to them is never a real scope violation. Also confirmed by F024's round-4 reviewer as unchanged across every round of that PR, suggested folding into this same ticket rather than filing separately. Fixed: /dev/* write targets are now exempted from the scope check entirely; the 2>&1 idiom is fixed by two coordinated changes (segments_of() no longer fragments ">&", and strip_redirects() now recognizes and strips the fd-duplication form itself). ROUND 2 (adversarial review of PR #53): the original /dev/* exemption matched any path starting with '/dev/', which silently allowed two real writes: /dev/shm/* (a writable tmpfs on Linux, where this template runs in CI) and bash's /dev/tcp network-redirect extension (a live egress channel, not a device node). Narrowed to an enumerated allowlist (DEV_EXEMPT_EXACT: null/zero/stdout/stderr/tty) plus a /dev/fd/N pattern match. Also corrected strip_redirects()'s fd-dup comment, which overstated the stripped form as any '[n]>&word' -- real bash's >&word with a non-numeric word is an ordinary FILE redirect (&>word), not fd duplication; the CODE was already correctly restricted to digits/'-', only the comment was wrong. Filed F034 for the identical &-splitting bug in the sibling hook commit-gate.sh.template, where it is a REAL gate bypass (not just a false positive) -- deliberately not fixed in this PR (different file). ROUND 3 (adversarial review of PR #53): a comment claiming normalize()-before-exemption ordering was 'load-bearing' against traversal laundering was itself wrong once the exemption narrowed to exact-set/pattern membership (round 2) -- /dev/../etc/passwd was never going to match is_dev_exempt() regardless of ordering, since it resolves to /etc/passwd, not a member of the exempt set. Confirmed by mutation-testing the ordering claim itself: moving the check before normalize() changed zero assertions. Corrected the comment to describe the real reason normalize() runs first (recognizing equivalent spellings like /dev//null), and renamed the traversal test to describe what it actually pins (a plain F026 traversal-resolution regression, not an ordering dependency). Filed F036 for a third, unrelated pre-existing gap found in the same review: `>&word` (fd omitted, non-numeric word) is a real bash FILE redirect this hook's regex never recognizes at all, so the write target is never checked. ROUND 4 (adversarial review of PR #53): round 3's replacement comment/test-name for the /dev/../etc/passwd test still overstated what it pins -- disabling normalize()'s traversal resolution alone leaves it green, since both spellings are out of scope either way. The test actually pins the CONJUNCTION of exact-set membership and normalize-before-exemption ordering (reverting either alone leaves it green; reverting both together fails it). Corrected the comment and renamed the assertion to 'a /dev/../ traversal cannot launder a path into the /dev exemption'. Also dropped a platform-ambiguous example (/dev/fd/../null -- real devfs on macOS, but /dev/fd is a symlink to /proc/self/fd on Linux) from the equivalent-spellings comment, and folded two more real bypass forms found in the same review into F036's description (the space-separated `>& /etc/passwd` and quoted `>&'file'` forms).
approaches_tried: Two independent root causes, fixed together since both were needed to close the ticket's confirmed shapes: (1) /dev/null exemption -- main() now skips any write target whose normalized path starts with "/dev/", exempting the whole /dev/* namespace rather than an enumerated device list. (2) 2>&1 fd-duplication idiom -- two changes were both required: segments_of() no longer splits on a literal "&" when it immediately follows ">" (real bash lexes ">&" as one operator, not a redirect followed by a background "&"), and strip_redirects() gained a new leading regex alternative recognizing and stripping the "[n]>&word" form itself (fd duplication never writes to a file, so it can never be a real target) -- the segmentation fix alone was insufficient, since the un-fragmented "2>&1" would otherwise still leak into command_tokens as a bogus flagless target.

Mutation-tested each of the three independent code changes separately (reverting one at a time): each reversion fails exactly the assertions specific to that fix and nothing else (/dev/null exemption -> 3 failures; segmentation lookbehind alone -> 2 failures; strip_redirects fd-dup alternative alone -> the same 2 failures, confirming both changes are independently necessary for the 2>&1 case). Restored and re-verified 666/666 green after each.

Round 2: replaced the norm.startswith('/dev/') blanket exemption with an exact-set plus regex check (is_dev_exempt()), keeping normalize() running before the check so a /dev/../ traversal spelling can't launder a real out-of-scope path through it. Mutation-tested by reverting to the blanket startswith check: fails exactly the 2 new /dev/shm and /dev/tcp assertions.

(backslash included), not 'src/parser/..'. Same vulnerability class as F026 (path-traversal scope escape), different root cause (escape-character handling, not path resolution) -- one character added to a real, already-confirmed bypass.

features.notes: Discovered by F026's round-1 reviewer while stress-testing the traversal-resolution fix; explicitly flagged as pre-existing (not introduced by F026) and a different root cause, defensible as a follow-up rather than blocking F026's merge. Independently re-verified against real bash before filing (bash -c, not zsh, to get accurate shell semantics). Likely fix: strip backslash-escapes from a token (or from the whole segment before tokenizing) the same way quote characters are stripped, consistent with commit-gate.sh.template's existing posture on shell metacharacter handling.
approaches_tried: Confirmed the fix scope narrowly: the Edit/Write/MultiEdit legacy path receives file_path as a literal JSON string parameter, never shell-parsed, so backslash-escape semantics don't apply there -- only the Bash-command path (which reads shell command strings through segments_of()/unquote_token()) needed the fix. Applied backslash-unescaping (\X -> X) uniformly after quote-stripping in unquote_token(), accepting a documented residual (a real single-quoted literal backslash in a filename gets normalized away too) consistent with this hook's existing pattern-based, evadable-by-construction philosophy -- matches how other residuals in this same file are handled and documented.

features.description: skills/harness-init/enforce-scope.sh.template's unquote_token() strips the $'...' ANSI-C-quote wrapper (via a regex capturing its inner content) but never decodes the ANSI-C backslash escapes inside it, so a traversal segment spelled with a hex/octal escape survives intact. CONFIRMED against real bash: $'src/parser/\x2e\x2e/other/x.txt' really writes to src/other/x.txt (bash decodes \x2e to the literal character ".", twice, giving ".."), but the hook still sees the literal 8-character string \x2e\x2e as one path segment, which normalize() correctly does not recognize as "..", so it never resolves the traversal and the write is wrongly ALLOWED. Same vulnerability class and same consequence as F031 (a shell-level string-literal transformation the hook does not replicate, letting a traversal spelling evade normalize()'s exact ".." check), but a different mechanism: F031 was escape REMOVAL (\.. -> ..); this is escape DECODING (\x2e -> .) inside an already-recognized ANSI-C quote span. Pre-existing on main; NOT introduced or fixed by F031's PR (unquote_token's $' handling and its backslash-unescape pass are applied as two independent steps; the second never re-examines the already-extracted $'...' inner text for its own escape syntax).
features.coverage: n/a (shell suite, no coverage tooling; full_test 736/736 is the gate)
features.notes: Discovered by adversarial review of PR #50 (F031), explicitly filed as out-of-scope for that PR (a live bypass, unchanged by F031's fix, not a regression it introduced). Likely fix: after $'...' extraction, decode ANSI-C backslash escapes (\xHH, \NNN octal, \n, \t, etc. per bash's $'' grammar) before the existing plain-backslash unescape pass runs, or before normalize() sees the token -- scope this carefully, since decoding the wrong set of escapes could itself introduce a new gap. Fixed by decoding ANSI-C escapes in the same regex substitution that extracts the $'...' span. \cX (control-char), \uHHHH, and \UHHHHHHHH escapes are deliberately NOT decoded -- filed separately as F038 (same vulnerability class, narrower/rarer).
approaches_tried: Verified bash's actual $'...' escape-decoding rules empirically (bash 3.2.57) before implementing, rather than from memory: \xHH (1-2 hex digits, case-insensitive) and \nnn (1-3 octal digits) decode to that byte; \\, \', \", \a, \b, \e, \f, \n, \r, \t, \v decode to their usual meaning; any OTHER backslash escape (including \8/\9, invalid octal, or \x with no hex digit following) is left as a literal backslash plus that character UNCHANGED -- bash does not drop the backslash for an unrecognized escape inside $'...'.

Implemented _decode_ansi_c_escape() and wired it into unquote_token()'s existing $'...' extraction regex via a substitution callback, so decoding happens in the SAME pass that identifies the $'...' span -- not left for the generic outside-quotes backslash-unescape pass (F031) to run on undecoded escape text, which would have mangled it differently (e.g. turning \x2e into the wrong string x2e) rather than leaving the real vulnerability unaddressed.

Mutation-tested by reverting to the old plain-strip regex: exactly the 4 new DENY-path assertions fail (the two rc0-only assertions pass either way, since ALLOW also exits rc 0 -- matching the exact bug shape, a silent fail-open, not a crash). Restored and re-verified 736/736 green.

features.description: skills/harness-init/commit-gate.sh.template's has_staging_flag() only recognizes value-taking SHORT flags that REQUIRE a value (-m, -F, -t, -C, -c; NOT -S/-u, which real git treats as optargs whose bare form takes no value at all -- corrected here after F027 round 2 found the opposite claim was itself a bug) as consuming the following space-separated token as their value (F027). Long flags that take a space-separated value -- --message, --file, --author, --date, --template, --fixup, --squash, --reuse-message -- are not recognized at all, so the same bug class F027 fixed for short flags is still present for long flags. CONFIRMED against real git: `git commit --message -- -a` commits with subject '--' AND stages a dirty tracked file via the real trailing -a (a genuine stage-and-commit-in-one-step that the gate currently ALLOWS); `git commit --message -a` stages nothing extra (message text is literally '-a'), but the gate currently DENIES it as a false positive. Pre-existing on main, not introduced by F027 -- found during F027's PR #49 adversarial review, which scoped F027 itself to short-flag forms only rather than expanding that PR's diff to cover this too. Likely fix: a VALUE_TAKING_LONG_FLAGS set checked (as an exact-token match, not a per-character scan) before has_staging_flag's `tok.startswith("-") and not tok.startswith("--")` branch, mirroring the short-flag fix's skip-the-next-token approach -- and, per F027 round 2's finding, verify each long flag's actual git semantics (required-value vs. optarg) individually rather than assuming uniform behavior across the whole set.

features.notes: Discovered by adversarial review of PR #49 (F027). No Linear issue -- same precedent as F022-F031, internally discovered during review. ADDITIONAL ITEM (round-3 review of PR #49): -U/--unified <n> is a required-value short flag in neither VALUE_TAKING_SHORT_FLAGS nor REQUIRED_VALUE_SHORT_FLAGS, so `git commit -U -- -a` is technically misread the same way -m once was. Confirmed NOT currently exploitable: real git rejects a bare -U outright ("switch `U' expects an integer value"), so nothing stages regardless of the gate's verdict. Folded in here as a completeness item for whenever F032 is implemented, not urgent enough to fix on its own. ROUND 2 (adversarial review of PR #56): round 1 was itself incomplete in two ways confirmed by a mechanical sweep (1859 long-option-shaped strings extracted from the git binary, filtered to the subset git-commit recognizes -- round 2's own independent re-derivation found this understated the real count: git commit actually accepts 77 base long-option spellings plus the whole `--no-no-*` double-negation family (19 more), not merely 57; git's option space is also NOT a simple prefix tree, so walking prefixes alone prunes valid families like `--no-no-verify` while `--no-no` itself stays unrecognized -- the round-1 sweep's CONCLUSIONS (the two live bypasses, the abbreviation gap) still hold under round 2's independent re-derivation, only the narrative around exactly how many options exist was imprecise), each probed for a real stage-and-commit via `-- -a`): (1) --trailer was a live bypass, missing entirely (`git commit --trailer -- -a` genuinely stages and commits, identical to the original --message bug); 5 more value-taking flags (--reedit-message, --cleanup, --unified, --inter-hunk-context, --pathspec-from-file) were also missing, though none independently exploitable via `-- -a` (git rejects `--` as their value) -- added anyway for defense-in-depth consistency with the other 9. (2) Exact-token matching missed git's own prefix-abbreviation feature entirely, defeating the fix even for --message itself: `--mess`, `--messa`, `--messag`, `--trail`, `--traile` all genuinely resolve and stage+commit in real git. Fixed by replacing exact-set matching with _resolve_long_flag(), mirroring real git's own unambiguous-prefix rule against the full GIT_COMMIT_LONG_OPTIONS universe -- which also required a SECOND mechanical extraction pass beyond `--git-completion-helper` (whose own suggestion list omits real options like --allow-empty/--allow-empty-message entirely), done here by systematically probing every 2- and 3-letter prefix against real git and harvesting every name mentioned in its own 'ambiguous option' error messages. As a direct consequence, an abbreviated STAGING flag (e.g. --inc for --include) is now also recognized, closing a related gap the original exact-match STAGING_FLAGS check never covered either. ROUND 2 (adversarial review of PR #56): independently re-derived the full option set from git's own errors (not just --git-completion-helper/prefix-probing) and validated the disambiguation model against real git's unique/ambiguous verdict on all 536 recognized prefixes with zero mismatches -- confirmed VALUE_TAKING_LONG_FLAGS and GIT_COMMIT_LONG_OPTIONS are both exactly right (no missing, no bogus entries) and a 536-spelling x 2-attack-shape differential fuzz against real git found zero bypasses. Two follow-ups applied: (1) added 5 pinning tests for the defense-in-depth-only flags (--reedit-message/--cleanup/--unified/--inter-hunk-context/--pathspec-from-file), previously uncovered by any assertion since none is exploitable via `-- -a` -- pinned via the other direction instead (each genuinely consumes a bare '-a' as its own value in real git, confirmed by direct execution, so a command shaped this way must ALLOW). (2) GIT_COMMIT_LONG_OPTIONS is a second git-version-pinned table in this file without a residual-holes entry alongside GIT_FLAGS_WITH_VALUE's existing one -- noted here as the retirement condition per this repo's own rule: if a future git version changes which options are ambiguous with which (e.g. adds a new option sharing a prefix with an existing one), GIT_COMMIT_LONG_OPTIONS needs re-verification against that version; last verified against git 2.52.0.
approaches_tried: Verified each of the 8 named long flags against `git commit -h` before implementing: all shown as required-value (`<value>`), none using the bracketed optarg syntax `--untracked-files[=<mode>]` uses -- so, unlike F027's -S/-u split, no attached-vs-required distinction was needed here. Added VALUE_TAKING_LONG_FLAGS as an exact-token-match set and one new branch in has_staging_flag()'s existing loop: a bare match consumes the next token as an opaque value, mirroring the short-flag mechanism exactly. The attached "--message=foo" form is a distinct string that never matches the exact-token check, so it needed no special-casing.

Mutation-tested by removing the new branch: exactly the 10 new assertions fail (9 DENY cases plus the --message "-a" false-positive fix), confirming they catch the bug. Restored and re-verified 745/745 green.

Round 2: mechanically extracted the full git-commit long-option list via two passes (git commit --git-completion-helper, then a systematic ambiguous-prefix probe against real git covering every 2- and 3-letter combination) rather than trust either source alone -- the second pass caught two real options (--allow-empty, --allow-empty-message) the first source omitted entirely. Added _resolve_long_flag() implementing real git's own unambiguous-prefix resolution rule (a prefix resolves only if it matches exactly one name in the full option universe; an ambiguous prefix returns None, matching real git's own behavior of erroring out and running nothing, so treating an ambiguous prefix as unrecognized here is always safe). Wired into has_staging_flag() for BOTH the value-taking long-flag check and the staging-flag (--all/--include) check, replacing the narrower exact-match-only version. Mutation-tested by reverting to the exact-match-only version: fails exactly the 6 new abbreviation-specific assertions.

features.description: skills/harness-init/enforce-scope.sh.template's cp_mv_targets() and sed_inplace_targets() compare flag tokens RAW (e.g. `tok in TARGET_DIRECTORY_FLAGS`, `tok.startswith("-t")`, `tok in SED_SCRIPT_VALUE_FLAGS`), so quoting a flag evades flag recognition entirely: `cp "-t" "src/other/d/" src/parser/a` and `cp '-t' src/other/d/ src/parser/a` are both wrongly ALLOWED (real bash writes to src/other/d/, an out-of-scope destination named via -t, but the quoted '-t' token never matches TARGET_DIRECTORY_FLAGS so cp_mv_targets() falls through to last_flagless_token() and picks the wrong argument as the destination). Same shape for `cp "--target-directory=src/other/d/" src/parser/a` and `sed "-i" "" -e "s/a/b/" src/other/f.txt` (real sed writes src/other/f.txt). Same vulnerability family as F023/F024/F025/F028 -- a shell-level transformation (here, quote removal on a FLAG token, not a target token) that these two extractors don't replicate before comparing against their flag sets.

features.notes: Discovered by adversarial review of PR #51, round 2 (F028's split_tokens() fix). Explicitly filed as a separate, pre-existing bug (identical on main and the F028 branch), not a regression from that PR. Likely fix, per the reviewer: the sibling hook commit-gate.sh.template already solved this (commit-gate.sh.template:389, `tokens = [unquote_token(t) for t in split_tokens(seg)]`, with a comment explicitly stating tokens must be split then unquoted one at a time, never the reverse -- F025). IMPORTANT TRAP flagged by the same reviewer: the obvious one-line port of that fix would be WRONG here, because unquote_token() is not idempotent since F031 added backslash-stripping (e.g. 'src/other/a\\b.txt' unquoted once is 'src/other/a\b.txt', unquoted TWICE becomes 'src/other/ab.txt'). write_targets() already maps unquote_token over its final target list, and redirect_targets() output bypasses split_tokens() entirely -- so unquoting at split time would double-unquote command-token targets while single-unquoting redirect targets, silently undoing F031's traversal defense. Safe shape (per the reviewer): derive an unquoted VIEW of each token for flag detection only (cp_mv_targets()/sed_inplace_targets()' own comparisons), keep the raw quoted tokens for target extraction, and leave the existing single unquote_token map in write_targets() untouched. ROUND 2 (adversarial review of PR #59): the claim that a quoted "--" was 'the same pre-existing residual' those functions already had was WRONG -- it was a NEW fail-open regression this round-1 fix itself introduced. Before round 1, a quoted "--" was invisible to BOTH the separator check and the flag checks (raw '"--"' doesn't start with '-'), which was self-consistent (just always wrong the same way). Once flag checks became view-aware but the '"--"' check stayed raw, the two disagreed: a quoted "--" (e.g. `cp "--" "-t" src/parser/d/ src/other/x`, or `sed -i "--" -i src/other/f.txt`) is just as real a separator to the receiving command as an unquoted one (the shell strips quotes before argv is built), but the hook's separator check never saw it, letting the real destination past it go unchecked -- a genuine fail-open, confirmed via ground-truth bash/cp/sed execution, not merely a naming inaccuracy. Fixed by making the "--" check view-aware in ALL FOUR places that independently implement it: all_flagless_tokens(), cp_mv_targets(), _separator_index(), and sed_inplace_targets()'s own loop -- doing only some of the four (as round 1 did for cp_mv_targets()/sed's loop but not all_flagless_tokens()) reintroduces the same class of guard-vs-check disagreement F029 round 3 already closed once, just via a different trigger. Also added test coverage for 5 previously-mutation-uncovered comparisons the same review found (_separator_index's own "--" check, the empty-suffix check via an ANSI-C $'' spelling that never matches the old literal markers, cp's attached "-tDIR" whole-quoted form, and the loop's SED_SCRIPT_VALUE_FLAGS and generic-dash checks) -- each now has a dedicated, hand-verified discriminating test, not just suite-wide green. Filed F040 for a separate, wider gap the same review found: write_targets() compares the COMMAND NAME itself raw (`\\rm`/`"rm"`/`'rm'` all evade recognition entirely), deliberately not fixed here to keep this round's diff focused on the "--" regression. ROUND 3 (adversarial review of PR #59): confirmed B1/B2/B3 fixed and execution-verified (the backslash sweep that found 70 fail-opens in round 2 now finds 0; both previously-surviving B2 mutants now killed by dedicated assertions). Also independently constructed and verified the false-positive-direction test I'd declined to attempt in round 2 (`cp -tsrc/parser/\\../other/x src/parser/a.txt`, a double-backslash case where a literal `\..` directory component survives and the real destination stays under src/parser/ -- confirmed ALLOW, correctly). Two new findings: (N1, required) the --target-directory= branch of _attached_value_raw() had ZERO mutation coverage -- reverting ONLY that branch to view-slicing survived 807/807 untouched, reintroducing the B1 fail-open on that one path; the prior round's mutation claim held only for the -tDIR branch, not both. Fixed with a matching backslash-bearing --target-directory= regression test (ground-truthed against real gcp), mutation-tested. (N2, required) the existing quoted '-tDIR' assertion passed by substring accident: two more helper mutants (deleting the quote-skipping branch entirely; an off-by-one at the split point) both survived 807/807 because the resulting wrong value "tsrc/other/d/" still contains "src/other/d/" as a substring. Anchored the assertion on the denial message's "write to '...'" quote boundary, which now kills both. (N3, disclosed, not fixed) a genuinely new-vs-main false-positive shape: a backslash-escaped character inside the FLAG PREFIX itself (not the value) throws off the raw-token walk's character count by one per escape (`cp -\\tsrc/parser/x`, `cp $'-t'src/parser/x`, `cp --target-\\directory=src/parser/x` -- all genuinely in-scope, wrongly denied; 18/112 brute-forced spellings, zero fail-opens, strictly over-denial). Documented as a residual in _attached_value_raw()'s own docstring rather than fixed: nobody escapes characters inside a bare flag name in practice, and closing it needs escape-state tracking through the prefix walk itself. (N4) the helper's empty-string fallback return was initially flagged as unreachable dead code (brute-forced 597,870 tokens, zero cases reach it) -- kept in place after the reviewer tested the ACTUAL failure mode of removing it and confirmed it isn't cosmetic: an implicit None return would make write_targets()'s later unquote_token(None) raise TypeError, crashing the hook's python; the bash wrapper then captures an empty DENY_REASON, so the hook silently ALLOWS. The defensive return prevents a crash-induced silent fail-open, not a style preference -- both call sites guarantee it's unreachable in practice, but the cost of that guarantee ever being wrong is asymmetric (silent bypass vs. one harmless line), which is why it stays. (N5) merged origin/main (F014, the docs catch-up, and their features.json entries) -- resolved by keeping the array as git's own 3-way merge produced it (no overlapping entries) and recomputing total_features/passing from the final array. (N6) adopted F034's drift-resistant coverage wording instead of a fixed count, since this field would otherwise go stale the moment main's total changes again (as happened between rounds 2 and 3: 807 -> 823 -> 898).
approaches_tried: Added _flag_view(tok) = unquote_token(tok), used ONLY for flag-recognition comparisons in cp_mv_targets() and sed_inplace_targets() -- never returned or stored as the target/token itself, which stays raw so write_targets()'s existing single unquote_token() pass at the very end still unquotes it exactly once. This avoids the double-unquote trap the F028-round-2 reviewer flagged (unquote_token() is not idempotent since F031's backslash-stripping).

For cp_mv_targets(): the bare "-t DIR"/"--target-directory DIR" forms return the RAW next token (tokens[i+1], completely untouched -- safe by construction). RETRACTED (round-2 review of PR #59 caught this claim as false of the shipped code): this entry originally said the "--" check "stays on the raw token" and that a quoted "--" was "a separate, undocumented residual, not part of this fix" -- both wrong; round 2 (see approaches_tried[5]/[6]) made the "--" check view-aware in all four sites, closing it as a real fix, not a residual. The attached "--target-directory=DIR"/"-tDIR" forms originally extracted their value from the VIEW, framed here as "a documented, narrower residual"; round 2 proved that framing wrong too (it flips scope decisions in BOTH directions vs. main -- a regression, not a residual) and replaced it with _attached_value_raw() (see approaches_tried[6]).

For sed_inplace_targets(): every flag comparison (the two any() guards, and the loop's SED_SCRIPT_VALUE_FLAGS/-i/generic dash checks) now compares against the view. Also had to fix _separator_index() to use the SAME view-based comparison for its own SED_SCRIPT_VALUE_FLAGS check -- otherwise a quoted "-e"/"-f" would make the guards and the separator-finding walk disagree about where flag parsing ends, reintroducing the exact guard-vs-loop mismatch class F029 round 3 already fixed for a different trigger (a value-consumed "--" there; a quoted flag here).

Caught and fixed one bug of my own during implementation: the "-i ''" BSD empty-suffix check originally compared the VIEW against EMPTY_STRING_TOKENS ("''"/'""'), but those two literal strings are exactly what unquote_token() strips AWAY (a view of "''" is the empty string "", never equal to the 2-char marker). Fixed by checking `_flag_view(next_token) == ""` directly -- a strictly more general check that also handles any other empty-string spelling (e.g. $''''), and removed the now-dead EMPTY_STRING_TOKENS constant.

Mutation-tested both fixes independently: reverting cp_mv_targets() to raw comparisons fails exactly its 6 new assertions; reverting sed_inplace_targets()'s two any() guards to raw comparisons fails 2 assertions, BOTH belonging to the -i guard (round-2 review corrected this entry: the has_explicit_script guard contributed zero coverage at the time this was written -- see approaches_tried[7]/finding B2). Restored and re-verified 798/798 green after each (the total has grown since; see the header total_features/passing fields and this feature's own coverage field for the current count, not this historical note).

Round 2: made the "--" check view-aware in all_flagless_tokens(), cp_mv_targets(), _separator_index(), and sed_inplace_targets()'s loop (4 sites, previously only 2 of the 4 were fixed and the other 2 were left deliberately raw based on an incorrect 'pre-existing residual' framing). Added 3 new regression tests for the confirmed fail-opens (quoted "--" for cp, for sed, and a discriminating rm-based test isolating all_flagless_tokens() specifically from cp_mv_targets()'s own independent "--" handling) plus 5 more closing every mutation-coverage gap the same review identified (_separator_index, the ANSI-C empty-suffix spelling, cp's attached -tDIR form, and the loop's two remaining raw comparisons). Mutation-tested all 8 new/changed comparisons independently: each reversion to a raw comparison fails exactly its own dedicated assertion(s) and nothing else.

Round 2 follow-up, PR #59 round-2 review (execution-grounded: GNU coreutils cp/mv/rm 9.11 plus BSD cp/sed, mutation-tested all 14 view-vs-raw comparisons, a 3.7M-command unquoted sweep, and a depth-3 quoted sweep with 7,630 execution-verified cases): (B1, blocking) cp_mv_targets()'s two ATTACHED-value branches (--target-directory=DIR, -tDIR) extracted their value from the VIEW -- an already-unquoted-and-unescaped string -- which write_targets()'s later single unquote_token() pass then processed a SECOND time. Since unquote_token() isn't idempotent (F031), this silently mis-resolved any backslash in the destination in BOTH directions (measured over 3,645 backslash-bearing -t destinations: 70 unquoted cases regressed DENY->ALLOW, a fail-open confirmed against real gcp -- `gcp -ts\\rc/parser/x a.txt` genuinely targets the literal directory `s\rc/parser/x`, not the in-scope-looking `src/parser/x` the old code produced; 1,376 regressed ALLOW->DENY). Fixed with a new _attached_value_raw() helper: since unquote_token() strips quote characters from anywhere in a token (not just matched edge pairs) and unescapes backslashes globally, it walks the RAW token counting non-quote characters until the recognized prefix length is consumed, returning the RAW (still possibly quoted/escaped) suffix for write_targets() to resolve in exactly one pass -- verified against every existing quoting shape (bare, whole-token-quoted, value-only-quoted) plus the new backslash regression test, and mutation-tested (reverting to view-slicing fails exactly the 2 new deny-form/target-name assertions). (B2, blocking) Two comparisons had zero mutation coverage: _separator_index()'s own SED_SCRIPT_VALUE_FLAGS check (a quoted "-f" consuming a literal "--" script-file name) and sed_inplace_targets()'s has_explicit_script guard -- the existing test for the latter used an IN-SCOPE target, so both correct and reverted code landed on the same observable ALLOW (one legitimately, one vacuously via the real target being swallowed as a fake implicit script). Added a discriminating out-of-scope-target test for each; mutation-tested (each revert now fails exactly its own new assertions, confirmed independently for both). (B3) Retracted a stale claim in approaches_tried[1] that no longer matched the shipped code (see that entry). Also corrected two stale test-count nits ("759/759" and "739/739") to the current 807/807.

features.description: skills/harness-init/enforce-scope.sh.template's redirect_targets()/strip_redirects() only recognize `>`/`>>` (file redirect) and `[n]>&(digits|-)` (fd duplication) as real redirect operators. Real bash also has `>&word` for a NON-numeric, non-'-' word (fd omitted) -- this is `&>word`, an ordinary FILE redirect, not fd duplication. CONFIRMED: `echo HELLO >&/etc/passwd` genuinely creates/overwrites /etc/passwd in real bash (bash 3.2.57), but this hook's regex never matches `>&` followed by a non-digit/non-'-' word at all, so the write target is never extracted and the command is wrongly ALLOWED -- confirmed identical on origin/main and after F030's fix (pre-existing, not a regression). Widening strip_redirects()'s existing `>&(?:\d+|-)` alternative to match any word would be WRONG (that alternative exists specifically to STRIP the fd-dup form without creating a bogus target, per F030's own comment); the real fix belongs in redirect_targets(), which needs a new alternative recognizing `>&word` (word not purely digits or '-') as a real file-redirect target, mirroring the existing `>>?` alternative. CONFIRMED by adversarial review of PR #53, round 3: two related forms also genuinely write a real file and also bypass this hook, unchanged on both main and the F030 branch -- the space-separated `>& /etc/passwd` (whitespace between `>&` and the word) and the quoted `>&'file'` form. Any fix for this feature must allow intervening whitespace/quoting between `>&` and the word, not just the bare-adjacent form the original description named, or it will miss both.
features.notes: Discovered by adversarial review of PR #53, round 2 (F030's narrowed /dev/* exemption and strip_redirects() comment fix). Confirmed pre-existing on main, unrelated to F030's own changes; lower severity than F034 (this hook's Bash coverage is explicitly documented as best-effort/pattern-based, not adversarial-proof, and this is an unusual redirect shape), so not urgent enough to block F030's merge.

features.description: skills/harness-init/enforce-scope.sh.template's sed_inplace_targets() recognizes GNU/BSD in-place editing only via a bare `-i`, an attached short-flag suffix (`t.startswith("-i")` on an UNCLUSTERED token, e.g. `-i.bak`), or `--in-place` exactly. Two real, ordinary invocation shapes are missed entirely: (1) CLUSTERED short flags, e.g. `sed -ri 's/a/b/' file` or `sed -ni 's/a/b/' file` (GNU allows combining -r/-n with -i in one token) -- `t.startswith("-i")` is false for `-ri`/`-ni` (the string starts with '-r'/'-n', not '-i'), so the whole in-place-presence guard misses it and sed_inplace_targets() returns [] unconditionally, wrongly ALLOWING an in-place edit of an out-of-scope file; (2) GNU's attached long-form suffix `--in-place=.bak` -- matches neither `t == "--in-place"` (exact match only) nor `t.startswith("-i")` (the token starts with `--`, not `-i`), same wrong-ALLOW outcome. CONFIRMED more reachable in ordinary usage than anything F029 itself fixed (no unusual quoting or '--' needed, just a common flag-combining habit).
features.notes: Discovered by adversarial review of PR #52, round 3 (F029's sed_inplace_targets() separator-index fix). Confirmed pre-existing on main, unrelated to F029's own '--' work -- a different bug class (clustered/long-form flag recognition, not '--' awareness). The existing header comment documents a clustered-flag residual for cp/mv (-rt DIR) only; sed has no equivalent note today, which this feature's fix should also add once landed. Likely fix: recognize any short-flag cluster containing 'i' as specifying in-place mode (mirroring commit-gate.sh's own cluster-scanning approach, F027), and recognize `--in-place=` as an attached-value prefix alongside the exact `--in-place` match. Also noted (round-4 review of PR #52, non-blocking): a pre-existing over-deny, identical on main and unrelated to any F029 change -- `sed -f -i.bak file` denies, since the in-place guard's -e/-f VALUE scan sees the string '-i.bak' and its own startswith('-i') check misfires on it, even though real sed treats '-i.bak' here as -f's script-file VALUE (an unusual but valid filename) and writes nothing. Fails safe (over-deny on an absurd filename), so not urgent, but worth folding into whichever fix lands for this feature's own -ri/--in-place= gaps.

features.description: skills/harness-init/commit-gate.sh.template's command_segments() splits on any literal '&' (re.finditer(r"\|\||&&|[|;\n&]", masked)), including the one glued to '>' in the fd-duplication idiom '2>&1' -- the identical bug F030 fixed in the SIBLING hook (enforce-scope.sh.template's segments_of()), but here it is a REAL gate bypass, not just a usability false-positive. CONFIRMED: 'git commit 2>&1 -am "x"' splits into segments ['git commit 2>', '1 -am "x"'] -- the '-am' staging flag lands in the SECOND segment, whose first token is '1', not 'git'/'commit', so segment_subcommand() never recognizes it as a git-commit segment at all and has_staging_flag() never runs on it. check_compound_stage_and_commit() returns ALLOW on a command that genuinely stages and commits in one step in real bash (confirmed: 'echo 2>&1 -am "x"' really does print '-am x' to stdout, proving the remaining arguments reach the command after the mid-command redirect, exactly as real bash parses it). The same one-character lookbehind fix F030 applied to enforce-scope.sh's segments_of() (change the split regex's bare '&' alternative to '(?<!>)&', so '&' is only a separator when NOT immediately preceded by '>') closes this too. CONFIRMED (round-2 review of PR #53): the separated form 'git commit 2>&1 -a -m "x"' bypasses identically to the '-am' cluster form -- not limited to the clustered flag shape.
features.coverage: n/a (shell suite, no coverage tooling; full_test is the gate -- count omitted here since it drifts on every sibling feature merge; see the header total_features/passing fields for the current count)
features.notes: Discovered by adversarial review of PR #53 (F030), which fixed the identical bug in the sibling hook enforce-scope.sh.template and found the same root cause here too, but classified as a real gate bypass rather than a usability false-positive since this hook's whole purpose is to deny compound stage-and-commit commands. Deliberately not fixed inside PR #53 (different file, would have been scope creep on that PR). Given the severity (a live bypass of shipped security infrastructure, same class as F025), prioritized above the other pending internally-discovered features. ROUND 2 CORRECTION: round 1's claim that a leftover redirect token is fully 'inert' to has_staging_flag() was wrong -- it can be silently consumed as a value-taking short flag's value (e.g. -m), shifting the token-position-dependent scan and causing a narrow, NEW false deny (`git commit -m 2>&1 -a`, which real git does not stage-and-commit, since bash's own redirect-stripping makes '-a' the message text, not a flag). Accepted as a documented residual (fail-closed, low severity) rather than building additional machinery to strip redirect fragments from the token stream before flag-scanning runs.
approaches_tried: Applied the identical one-character lookbehind fix F030 used in enforce-scope.sh.template's segments_of(): changed command_segments()'s split regex from a bare '&' inside the character class to a separate '(?<!>)&' alternative, so '&' is only a separator when NOT immediately preceded by '>'.

ROUND 2 (adversarial review of PR #58): round 1's claim that no second fix was needed, unlike F030, was PARTIALLY wrong. Two real issues found: (1) the mirror shape '&>'/'&>>' (bash's combined stdout+stderr redirect) was still a live, identical bypass -- `git commit &> out.log -a -m "x"` split into a segment starting with '>', never recognized as a git-commit segment. Fixed by making the lookaround symmetric: '(?<!>)&(?!>)'. (2) The 'inert leftover token' claim was also false: a leftover redirect fragment like '2>&1' CAN be consumed as a value-taking short flag's value (e.g. `git commit -m 2>&1 -a` treats '2>&1' as -m's value, then reads the real '-a' as a flag and DENIES) -- but real git, since bash also strips the redirect, sees `git commit -m -a` where '-a' becomes the MESSAGE TEXT, not a flag, so nothing stages and ALLOW is the correct verdict. This is a NEW, narrow FALSE DENY (fail-closed, not a bypass) introduced by round 1's own fix, accepted as a documented residual rather than building a full strip_redirects()-equivalent for commit-gate.sh: the severity is low (an inconvenience, never a security bypass) and this hook's own posture already accepts pattern-based, evadable-by-construction coverage for the same trade-off reasons enforce-scope.sh does.

Mutation-tested the &>/&>> fix: reverting the symmetric lookaround back to '(?<!>)&' alone fails exactly the 2 new assertions. Restored and re-verified 734/734 green at the time (post-merge count is 773/773; the assertion count grows as sibling branches merge).

features.description: skills/harness-init/enforce-scope.sh.template's ANSI_C_ESCAPE_PATTERN (F033) decodes \xHH and \nnn escapes inside a $'...' span but does not recognize \cX (control-char, e.g. \cA -> 0x01), \uHHHH (4-hex-digit Unicode codepoint), or \UHHHHHHHH (8-hex-digit Unicode codepoint) -- all three are real bash $'...' escape forms. A traversal segment spelled via one of these (e.g. \u002e\u002e for '..') would be left as literal, undecoded text by the current decoder (since it's treated as an 'unrecognized escape', matching the same 'leave backslash+char literal' fallback used for genuinely unknown escapes), so normalize() never sees a real '..' to resolve, while real bash WOULD decode it and genuinely escape scope -- the exact same vulnerability class as F033, just a narrower/rarer set of escape spellings. VERIFIED against this repo's actual bash (3.2.57): \u002e and \U0000002e are NOT decoded at all here (both left as literal backslash-plus-text, e.g. `$'a\u002eb'` prints literally `a\u002eb`) -- so \u/\U are not a live concern in THIS environment's bash version specifically, though the gap in this hook's own decoder remains real for any bash new enough to support them (believed added around bash 4.2, per documentation; UNVERIFIED in this environment, since no bash newer than 3.2.57 was available to test against directly -- found by adversarial review of PR #57). \cX (control-char) IS decoded by this bash (`$'a\cAb'` -> 0x01), but \cX escapes only ever produce non-printable control bytes (0x00-0x1F), which can never spell '.' (0x2e) or '/' (0x2f) -- so \cX's own gap in this hook's decoder, while real, is NOT independently traversal-exploitable the way \u/\U could be on a newer bash. Net: on THIS repo's bash, none of \c/\u/\U currently reaches a live bypass; the residual is worth closing for portability (a newer bash elsewhere) and completeness, not because it's exploitable here today.
features.notes: Discovered while implementing F033 (same feature, deliberately scoped out to keep that fix narrow and match the description's own confirmed exploit shapes). Likely fix: extend ANSI_C_ESCAPE_PATTERN with \c., \u{4 hex}, \U{8 hex} alternatives and their decode logic in _decode_ansi_c_escape(), verifying each against whatever bash version is available first (this repo's bash 3.2.57 may predate \u/\U support, added in a later bash version -- confirm before assuming the vulnerability is live here).

features.description: skills/harness-init/enforce-scope.sh.template's target-extraction pipeline does not truncate a token at an embedded NUL byte the way real bash truncates a word at its first NUL when building argv. CONFIRMED: `echo x > $'src/other/bad.txt\x00/../../parser/ok.txt'` -- real bash decodes \x00 to a genuine NUL byte and truncates the argument there, so the real write target is 'src/other/bad.txt' (OUT of scope), but this hook's normalize()/scope-check pipeline processes the WHOLE string (NUL and all), resolving the '..' segments after the NUL and landing on 'src/parser/ok.txt' (IN scope) -- wrongly ALLOWED. CONFIRMED as pre-existing on origin/main BEFORE F033 too (not a regression from F033's own fix); F033 makes this specific route more direct since \x00 now genuinely decodes to a real NUL byte inside a $'...' span, where previously the literal 4-character string '\x00' just stayed as inert text. Likely fix: truncate the token at the first NUL character (if any) immediately after unquote_token() finishes decoding, before normalize() or the scope-prefix comparison ever see it.
features.notes: Discovered by adversarial review of PR #57 (F033), explicitly confirmed as a pre-existing bypass unchanged by that PR (verified ALLOW on both origin/main before F033 and the F033 branch) -- filed alongside F038 per the reviewer's own recommendation, same general vulnerability class (a shell-level string transformation this hook's pipeline doesn't replicate before the scope check runs).

features.description: skills/harness-init/enforce-scope.sh.template's write_targets() compares the COMMAND NAME token (command_tokens[0]) RAW against ("cp","mv")/("tee","rm")/"sed", so quoting or backslash-escaping the command name itself evades recognition entirely, not just its flags or targets. CONFIRMED: `\rm src/other/f.txt`, `"rm" src/other/f.txt`, and `'rm' src/other/f.txt` are ALL wrongly ALLOWED (no target extracted at all, since the raw token is '\\rm'/'"rm"'/"'rm'", none of which equals the bare string "rm"), even though `\rm` (backslash-prefixed) is a common, everyday idiom for bypassing a shell alias named rm/cp/mv, not an adversarial evasion technique. Arguably a WIDER hole than F035 itself, since it defeats every command-type extractor (cp_mv_targets(), all_flagless_tokens() for tee/rm, sed_inplace_targets()) in one step, before any of their own (now-fixed) flag/target recognition logic even runs. Likely fix: compare _flag_view(command_tokens[0]) instead of the raw token, mirroring the same pattern used throughout F035 -- this is a command-name recognition check, not a target-value extraction, so no double-unquote risk applies (the command name itself is never returned as a target).
features.notes: Discovered by adversarial review of PR #59 (F035), during a systematic sweep for the same 'raw comparison evadable by quoting' bug class this feature's own fix addresses elsewhere in the same file. Confirmed identical on main and the F035 branch (pre-existing, not a regression). Verified directly: `\\rm src/other/f.txt` and `"rm" src/other/f.txt` both exit rc 0 with no permissionDecision field at all against a fixture scoped to src/parser/, i.e. a genuine silent bypass, not merely a misnamed denial.
